text:
Heavyweight Champion Jack Dempsey and leading contender Harry Wills sign to fight (circa June of 1925) on September 26th or October 4th or 5th (depending on the many confusing, convoluted and contradictory accounts and articles I have found).

The bout, in September or October of 1925, would likely have been an excellent matchup and in this photo they are each in Detroit signing articles of agreement for "The Manassa Mauler" to defend the World Heavyweight Championship against "The Black Panther."

As we all know, what would likely have been a fantastic match never came off.
---------------------------------------------------------
From the July 17th (1925) edition of The New York Times:

2 DEMPSEY BOUTS SIGNED BY RICKARD; Champion Agrees to Fight Wills Next Year and Probably Tunney in September.

Jack Dempsey, world's heavyweight champion, signed an agreement yesterday with Promoter Tex Rickard for two fights, one against Harry Wills, New Orleans negro challenger, and the other against Gene Tunney or any other aspirant whose qualifications will warrant the approval and support of the public. A formal contract is to be signed today. The Wills bout is out of the question for this year in the view of both Dempsey and Rickard, but the champion wants to meet Tunney this year in this city, if the State Athletic Commission will consent, or in Jersey City, if Rickard can promote the bout there without offending the commission. The date and other details of Dempsey's appearance this year were not divulged. Rickard said he wanted to promote a bout between Dempsey and possibly Tunney between Sept. 7 and 14 at the Yankee Stadium, or some time after Labor Day in Jersey City. Dempsey, according to Rickard, will visit the headquarters of the Madison Square Garden Corporation this morning at 11 o'clock, where the formalities for the two bouts will be signed. Rickard's agreement does not prevent the champion from engaging in another match. The indications are that Dempsey will consent to box Bartley Madden in Michigan City, Ind.. for Promoter Floyd Fitzsimmons late next month or on Labor Day, so that the prospects are that Dempsey will be in two matches this year.
Commission View in Doubt.
Whether the State Athletic Commission will countenance a meeting between Dempsey and Tunney this Fall remains to be seen. Chairman James A. Farley is out of town now and will not return until next week. Colonel John J. Phelan, Chairman of the License Committee, refused to believe that Rickard had proceeded with business arrangements with Dempsey in violation of an order of the commission forbidding promoters and matchmakers to discuss terms with the champion, who is on the ineligible list with Jack Kearns because of Dempsey's failure to recognize a challenge from Wills.
Commissioner William Muldoon likewise refused to believe that Rickard had carried on business with Dempsey against the wishes of the commission. Neither official, however, would stare what action, if any, the commission might take. Commissioner Muldoon said the matter probably would be undecided until the return of Chairman Farley. Rickard was not apprehensive. He pointed out that the ban against Dempsey is for the champion's refusal to recognize Wills's challenge. The fact that Dempsey, he said, consents to meet Wills in one of the two bouts amounts to an acceptance of Wills's challenge, and removes the occasion for the ban. The commission holds, however, that Dempsey must appear before the board and, without qualifications, consent to defend his title against Wills and post a substantial forfeit. Developments would be contingent on the disposition of the commission.
Dempsey Acts on His Own.
Dempsey announced his agreement with Rickard at the Hotel Alamac after his conference with him, and it was later confirmed by the promoter. The champion acted on his own initiative in accepting Rickard's proposition. This indicates that reports of a break with Kearns had been well founded. Rickard said he had conferred with Kearns before the latter's departure for the Coast last week, and that the manager had expressed satisfaction with the offer, subject to Dempsey's approval. However, Kearns signed no contracts, but Dempsey said he would receive his manager's third until their contract expires in September next year. This contract, the first between Dempsey and Kearns, was filed under the New York law, when Dempsey fought Luis Firpo here. Before that they went along on a fifty-fifty division of all of Dempsey's earnings. Dempsey and his opponents under present plans, will post substantial forfeits guaranteeing Wills a match with the champion next year, to provide against the emergency of Dempsey losing his title. This proposal will be submitted to the State Athletic Commission when the board reviews the Dempsey situation. Dempsey, however, is not convinced that a match with Wills will be permitted. He reiterated that sentiment for or against this match will decide whether it is to be held and added that he was perfectly willing to battle with Wills, Tunney or any other heavyweight who may be selected by promoters and supported by the public.
---------------------------------------------------------
In August (1925) Dempsey issued this statement:

"I still hold the same position in my attitude to the New York Boxing Commission, notwithstanding any consideration they have given my letters and telegram. In the matter of courtesy and decency I am going to remain the same.
"While I might object to receiving the official renderings of that particular boxing commission, well in advance in newspapers and wires before the commission met and discussed the matter, I still insist that I will fight Harry Wills, and if New York bars the world's championship fight I am open to propositions from boxing promoters elsewhere.
"I have met every exaction of the commission referred to and almost daily the situation is changed, and not by any impulsiveness or inadvisable notion will I enter into invited criticism of the New York Boxing Commission.
"There are two sides to all questions, and I am content to keep to the decent side, with the reiterated statement that I will fight Harry Wills and forego offers to fight any other man or men.
"If New York bars the possible match, the match is open to any or all promoters throughout the country.
"If Paddy Mullins, manager for Wills, still wants a match for the world's title he can operate with me or not, just as it suits him.
"Again let me say that my next fight will be with Harry Wills and I refrain from any solicited criticism of the New York Boxing Commission, whose desires I have met and which have been added to without any communication with me.
"That the New York Boxing Commission has in mind some certain club or promoter to stage this fight is a matter of deduction on the face of the returns.
"My proposition when in New York was to fight Harry Wills, as the commission insisted, and I never promised that I would return at a designated time to meet the commission personally. I did say that I could return and personally confer with the commission as a whole, and nothing has ever come from the commission naming a time when I should appear before them.
"Most of my information regarding the anticipated action of that commission has come from the newspapers and I have received no communication as request on demand from them.
"Of course, there is method in the official decree, but it is past me to do a lot of guessing. Again I say that I will fight Harry Wills for any promoter who can induce Paddy Mullins to sign for a match."
----------------------------------------------------------
There's been a lot of speculation, and innuendo, over the years about just why it never came off, but I'll rely on one of my favorite sources, The Fight City, written by Sean Crose in 2023, for their take on what may have been a great World Heavyweight Title fight:

Back during that awful time when for five long years it seemed Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao would never, ever meet in the ring, pundits and historians mused as to whether “MayPac” might be the biggest potential fight in boxing history to never materialize. Of course it did materialize and then many of us wished it had not, but in truth, if it hadn’t, it would have simply joined a long list of great matches that failed to take place. For example, what might have happened had iconic heavyweight champion Jack Dempsey and longstanding top contender Harry Wills ever clashed we will never know. Dempsey vs Wills will forever be the heavyweight superfight that never was.
Safe to assume it would have been one hell of a battle.
Yet Dempsey was almost modern in his inactivity. 
After winning the title by beating the tar out of Jess Willard in 1919, he competed just five times through the next five years. To put that into perspective, Danny Garcia, a contemporary often criticized for his lack of activity, has fought twice as often in the same span of time.
What Dempsey lacked in a full schedule, however, he made up for in ferocity and raw talent. For here was a new kind of fighter, a vicious ring assassin who set a savage pace, advancing relentlessly in his awkward crouch, which in fact made him deceptively hard to hit. Dempsey may not have been invincible – like Jack Johnson before him, he tasted defeat before winning the heavyweight crown – but he was a legitimate ring great with a wealth of hard-earned experience to support his high reputation. For example, after powerful Luis Firpo punched him out of the ring in the opening round of their savage brawl, Dempsey came back and knocked Firpo down and out the following round. He was a force to be reckoned with, no doubt.
Enter one Harry Wills, a Louisiana native known as “The Black Panther.” A man with a rectangular frame, Wills kicked around the heavyweight division for years, hoping to get a chance at the world title. He fought the great Sam Langford on many occasions and had also gotten the better of men who had likewise faced Dempsey, including the dangerous Firpo. And it’s worth noting that while Dempsey had to recover from a knockdown against “The Wild Bull of the Pampas,” Wills defeated the Argentinian with relative ease a year later.
But there was a major stumbling block to this worthy challenger meeting Dempsey in the ring, that being the simple fact that Wills happened to be black. 
From our particular vantage point in history, where people actually make sport of pretending to be offended by the innocuous, it’s hard to imagine blatant and public prejudice being tolerated, yet the racism of that day was very real. But ironically enough, Wills became so renowned and respected that even white America took a shine to him. Eventually people, including those in the media, started asking aloud what was so wrong about giving a deserving challenger a crack at the heavyweight crown.
In truth, Dempsey himself appeared willing to take Wills on, and for a whole lot of money, too. 
Those who argue that “The Manassa Mauler” drew the color line might be interested to know he did in fact sign a contract to meet Wills, and that he had fought black opponents before. The match, however, was simply not meant to be. The closest it may have come to actually occurring was in 1925. An agreement was reached with Wills getting fifty grand, a sizable purse at the time, but Dempsey’s much larger payment never came through. And thus neither did one of the most anticipated matches in history.
Instead, Dempsey fought and lost to Gene Tunney twice, the second time in insanely controversial fashion, while Wills went on to close out his career without a world title shot. 
To be sure, the “Phantom Title Fight,” Dempsey vs Wills, serves as a warning as to what happens when outside pressures and interests interfere with competition. 
Could Wills have bested Dempsey? 
It’s a good question. 
Had the two met in 1925 or 1926, which was the time when the match came closest to happening, Wills likely had a real chance. Then again …
To be sure, matters like this make for uncomfortable discussions. It’s not fun contemplating the widespread racism of the past, but it’s also difficult to grasp that things are not always as black and white as they may at first appear (pardon the pun). 
The truth is a number of factors prevented a Wills vs Dempsey match from taking place, one of them being Jack Johnson. “The Galveston Giant,” famed for his arrogant ways and his openly consorting with white women, so outraged white America during his turbulent reign that he virtually guaranteed that no title shot would be given to a black man for many years after.
Additionally, Wills likely hurt his cause by refusing to face Gene Tunney in a lucrative title eliminator that could have put even more pressure on those who could have made the fight happen. Reportedly Tunney was open to the match, but Wills turned it down. 
In the end, one thing is clear: both Wills and Dempsey were willing to face off in the ring. 
It’s easy to cast Dempsey as the villain here and think it was all too easy for him to avoid the match, but the evidence – including his signature – proves otherwise.
(Note from 20thCB:IM&M: Dempsey fought four black fighters during his career. Tunney, zero)
Years later, Dempsey told interviewer Peter Heller that the real obstacle was finding a venue. Presumably, there was simply too much widespread objection on the part of the people who had the means to stage the bout.
“They wouldn’t let you fight no place,” Dempsey told Heller in 1970. “Rickard wanted to make [it], but there was no place that you could put it on. … I wanted to fight him. … [But] they wouldn’t let you fight no place.”
It’s hard not to feel bad for Wills in all this. 
While Dempsey went on to iconic status, “The Black Panther,” despite his being an all-time great, is now largely forgotten. Though perhaps that was always meant to be the case. Perhaps Dempsey would indeed have prevailed had the two met in the ring. The fact we will never know is a blemish on the history of the sport. 
One brief side note: Wills reportedly ended up doing quite well for himself post-boxing in the real estate business.  The man always regretted, however, the fight that never was. And in that, he was not, and still isn’t, alone.

text:
Von Braun was ready to orbit a satellite in 1956 on a Redstone booster. The Administration stopped him.

"In 1955 the Stewart Committee and the Defense Department chose the Navy’s Project Vanguard over the Army–Navy Project Orbiter (von Braun’s Redstone-based proposal) as the U.S. International Geophysical Year satellite. The stated reasons included using a more “scientific,” less overtly military vehicle (the Viking-derived Vanguard rather than a ballistic missile associated with von Braun’s former V-2 team) so the first satellite would help establish the principle of free overflight of other countries’ territory—useful later for reconnaissance satellites. Eisenhower approved Vanguard; Orbiter was formally killed in September 1955.

In May 1956 the Defense Department explicitly told the Army not to plan or prepare any orbital use of Jupiter or Redstone hardware. On 20 September 1956 a Jupiter-C (a modified Redstone with upper stages) flew from Cape Canaveral on a re-entry test. It was close to orbital capability: with a live fourth stage and a small payload it could have reached orbit more than a year before Sputnik. Army Maj. Gen. John B. Medaris, von Braun’s superior at the Army Ballistic Missile Agency, telephoned him and ordered him personally to confirm that the fourth stage was inert, so the vehicle could not “accidentally” orbit. Contemporary accounts (including later reconstructions by historians such as T. A. Heppenheimer) treat that call as the direct operational block.

The Army itself wanted the launch and repeatedly offered Jupiter-C as a backup; it was not the source of the prohibition. State Department concerns about the legal and diplomatic appearance of a military first satellite fed into White House and NSC policy, but the binding orders von Braun received ran through the Pentagon. After Sputnik and the December 1957 Vanguard failure, Defense reversed course; von Braun’s team launched Explorer 1 on a Juno I (Jupiter-C derivative) on 31 January 1958."

text:
Today in History 
October 5th
1947
President Harry S. Truman made television history when he delivered the first presidential address televised from the White House. The broadcast represented an important milestone in American political communication, introducing a medium that would eventually transform the relationship between presidents and the public. Although television ownership was still relatively rare in 1947, Truman’s appearance demonstrated the growing potential of television to bring the president directly into American homes. (Truman Library)

Truman’s address came at a difficult moment in the aftermath of World War II. Much of Western Europe was still struggling to recover from the destruction of the war. Agricultural production had been severely affected by drought, floods, cold weather, and other problems, leaving millions of Europeans facing serious food shortages as winter approached. American leaders feared that widespread hunger could undermine Europe’s economic and political recovery. (Truman Library)

Speaking from the White House at 10:50 p.m., Truman asked Americans to participate voluntarily in a nationwide food-conservation campaign organized with the Citizens Food Committee. The goal was to reduce domestic consumption so that more grain and other food could be shipped overseas. Americans were asked to avoid meat on Tuesdays, avoid poultry and eggs on Thursdays, save a slice of bread every day, and request bread and butter at restaurants only when they actually intended to eat them. Farmers and businesses were also encouraged to reduce their use of grain. Truman announced that the White House, federal cafeterias, and the armed forces would participate in the conservation effort. (Truman Library)

The president argued that helping Europe was about more than humanitarian relief. He connected food assistance to the larger goal of rebuilding stable, self-supporting European democracies and securing a lasting peace. His appeal came as the United States was developing the broader European recovery program that became known as the Marshall Plan. Truman believed that long-term reconstruction would be threatened if European populations could not first survive the immediate shortages of food and other necessities. (Truman Library)

The October 5 broadcast was significant for another reason: it offered Americans an early glimpse of television’s future role in national politics. Radio remained the dominant electronic medium, and Truman’s address was simultaneously carried by radio, but television was beginning to expand rapidly. Future presidents would increasingly rely on televised speeches, press conferences, debates, campaign appearances, and national addresses to communicate directly with millions of citizens.

Truman himself would continue to play a role in television history. His 1949 inauguration became the first presidential inauguration to be televised, further demonstrating how quickly the new technology was entering American public life. The October 5, 1947 address therefore stands at the intersection of two major developments of the postwar era: America’s growing involvement in rebuilding Europe and the emergence of television as a powerful force in American politics and culture. #OTD

text:
FULL DD: $ASTS 🚀

It's been a while since I've done a big DD write up. I've been watching the hype around $ASTS, so I wanted to dig in myself and share what I found with everyone.

AST SpaceMobile is one of the more interesting RiskOn names in the market because the thesis has evolved from:

"Can this technology actually work?"

to:

"Can AST execute the constellation rollout fast enough to justify the valuation?"

Those are two very different questions.

Here's my current unbiased DD on $ASTS 👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛰️ WHAT IS AST SPACEMOBILE?

AST is building a satellite network designed to provide broadband directly to normal, unmodified smartphones.

No Starlink dish.
No special satellite phone.
No separate hardware.

The goal is essentially to turn space into an extension of terrestrial cellular infrastructure.

AST partners with existing mobile network operators rather than trying to replace them.

That distinction matters.

Partners/customers have included companies such as AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone and other major global carriers.

AST now says it has relationships with 60+ MNOs collectively covering more than 3 BILLION subscribers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 THE BULL CASE

1️⃣ THE TECHNOLOGY IS INCREASINGLY DE-RISKED

This isn't just a PowerPoint company anymore.

AST has successfully demonstrated direct-to-device connectivity and has continued launching its next-generation BlueBird satellites.

Its Block 1 system demonstrated a peak download speed of 98.9 Mbps directly to an ordinary smartphone.

The next-gen BlueBird architecture is designed for substantially more capacity.

Technical feasibility was arguably the largest existential risk several years ago.

That risk has fallen dramatically.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2️⃣ SATELLITE DEPLOYMENT IS FINALLY ACCELERATING

BlueBird 6 launched Dec 2025.

BlueBird 7 launched Apr 2026.

BlueBirds 8-10 launched June 2026.

BlueBirds 11-13 launched August 2026.

And AST has BlueBird 17 through 46 in various stages of production/assembly (per company Q2 2026 update).

This is important because ASTS eventually needs dozens of satellites, not a handful, before the revenue model really starts working at scale.

Execution is becoming the story now.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

3️⃣ THE ADDRESSABLE MARKET IS ENORMOUS

There are billions of cellular subscribers globally, but terrestrial networks still leave enormous geographic coverage gaps.

AST doesn't need consumers to replace their carrier.

The carrier can theoretically offer satellite coverage as an extension of the subscriber's existing plan.

That gives AST potential exposure to:

• Consumer connectivity
• Emergency coverage
• Rural broadband
• Maritime
• Aviation
• IoT
• Government/Defense
• Disaster response

AST estimates its MNO relationships already represent 3B+ subscribers.

Even extremely small ARPU economics across that user base could eventually become significant.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4️⃣ THE BUSINESS MODEL COULD HAVE MASSIVE OPERATING LEVERAGE

Building the constellation is brutally expensive.

But once deployed, incremental network usage theoretically becomes much more attractive economically.

AST isn't building thousands of retail stores or acquiring customers one at a time.

Its distribution partners already have the customers.

If the model succeeds:

Carrier owns customer relationship
↓
AST provides satellite infrastructure
↓
Revenue shared between the two

That could eventually become an incredibly scalable model.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

5️⃣ CONTRACTED REVENUE IS STARTING TO MATTER

AST reported approximately:

$1.3 BILLION

in aggregate contracted revenue commitments / government awards (Q2 2026 company backlog).

That doesn't equal $1.3B of recognized revenue today.

But it matters because AST is gradually moving from:

Technology demonstration

→ contracts

→ satellite deployment

→ commercial service

→ recurring revenue.

That's exactly the progression bulls needed to see.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

6️⃣ GOVERNMENT/DEFENSE COULD BECOME A SECOND MAJOR BUSINESS

This part of the ASTS thesis gets overlooked.

A large phased-array satellite network capable of connecting ordinary devices has obvious national security applications.

Remote communications.
Resilient communications.
Disaster environments.
Contested infrastructure.
Military operations.

Commercial cellular may be the headline opportunity.

Government could become a meaningful second revenue engine.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔥 THE RISKON ARGUMENT

This is where $ASTS gets particularly interesting.

ASTS has:

• Huge TAM
• Massive narrative potential
• Space exposure
• Telecom exposure
• Defense optionality
• Rapid revenue growth potential
• High beta
• High short interest (~24% of float)
• Major binary catalysts

That's basically the recipe institutions and retail traders tend to chase when liquidity starts flowing aggressively into higher-risk growth equities.

ASTS currently carries a beta around 2.7.

Translation:

When RiskOn works, ASTS can REALLY move.

But that works both directions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔴 NOW THE BEAR CASE

This isn't a cheap stock.

At ~$58, ASTS carries a market cap of roughly $23B while current revenue remains tiny compared with the eventual business investors are pricing in.

You're paying for future execution.

A LOT of future execution.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1️⃣ EXECUTION RISK

AST needs to manufacture, launch and successfully operate dozens more satellites.

Manufacturing delays matter.

Launch delays matter.

Deployment failures matter.

Satellite failures matter.

Regulatory delays matter.

Ground infrastructure delays matter.

Every quarter matters.

This remains one of the largest risks.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2️⃣ CAPITAL INTENSITY

Space infrastructure is expensive.

AST has dramatically strengthened its balance sheet (pro forma cash over $3.7B after the July 2026 convertible notes), but building a global constellation still requires enormous capital expenditure.

If deployment costs rise significantly or commercialization takes longer than expected, additional financing becomes possible.

That creates dilution/debt risk.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

3️⃣ VALUATION

This is probably the strongest bear argument.

Traditional valuation metrics look absurd because AST hasn't reached commercial scale yet.

Current investors are effectively underwriting what AST could earn several years from now.

If execution stays ahead of expectations, that can work.

If commercialization slips 12-24 months?

The valuation can compress FAST.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4️⃣ COMPETITION

The elephant in the room:

SpaceX / Starlink.

AST arguably has architectural advantages for broadband direct-to-device connectivity, but betting against SpaceX's ability to innovate would be foolish.

Other competitors and satellite providers are entering D2D as well.

This market could ultimately support multiple networks.

But AST does NOT have the battlefield to itself.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

5️⃣ REGULATORY + SPECTRUM RISK

Satellite telecommunications touches:

• FCC approvals
• Spectrum rights
• International regulators
• Carrier agreements
• Interference rules
• Space licensing

AST's carrier partnerships are a major advantage here.

But global rollout remains complicated.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

6️⃣ EXPECTATIONS ARE ALREADY HIGH

This might be the most important point.

$ASTS doesn't need to simply succeed.

At this valuation, it needs to succeed BIG.

There's a major difference.

The market already understands the opportunity.

Future returns increasingly depend on execution beating expectations rather than investors simply discovering the story.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💰 FINANCIAL PICTURE

2026 revenue is finally ramping.

Q2 revenue: ~$31.5M

But AST remains deeply loss-making while constellation deployment accelerates (Q2 net loss attributable to common ~$231M).

That isn't necessarily surprising for this stage of the buildout.

What matters now is:

Revenue acceleration
Satellite deployment
Cash burn
CapEx
Commercial activation
Subscriber adoption

Those are the numbers I'll be watching much more closely than EPS over the next several quarters.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🏦 WALL STREET

Analysts remain extremely divided.

Current targets roughly span (sources vary):

🐻 Low: ~$42.50
🎯 Consensus: ~$80-87
🐂 High: ~$108

That's a HUGE range.

Which tells you something important:

Nobody really knows yet what this business should be worth.

The difference between the bull and bear valuation models comes down primarily to:

Deployment speed
Subscribers
ARPU
Margins
Capital requirements
Commercialization timing

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📉 THE CHART

$ASTS closed around $58.45 (Oct 2, 2026).

And unlike the fundamental story, the technical picture isn't particularly bullish yet.

The stock remains below its shorter moving averages clustered around roughly:

$61-$63

(20DMA ~$61, 50DMA ~$63; 200DMA much higher around ~$81)

So while I'm fundamentally bullish on the long-term opportunity, I wouldn't pretend the chart has confirmed RiskOn again yet.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 MY $ASTS LEVELS

CURRENT: ~$58.45

🟢 SUPPORT

$57-58
Immediate support / current battle zone.

$55
Major near-term support + significant options positioning.

$52-53
Important structural support.

$49-50
Major support / near the 52-week low (~$49.31).

Lose $49 decisively and the technical thesis deteriorates substantially.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔴 RESISTANCE

$60-61
First major reclaim.

Also where short-term moving averages begin clustering.

$62.50-$65
IMO the most important near-term zone.

50DMA (~$63) + previous resistance + significant options positioning.

A strong reclaim of $65 changes the character of this chart.

$67-70
Next major supply area.

Above $70 with volume?

Now things start getting interesting.

Then:

$75

$85

$100+

are the levels I'd watch if RiskOn momentum returns.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🧭 MY BASE CASE

Below $55:

Defensive.

$55-$60:

Range / chop zone, for me.

Above $60:

Improving.

Above $65:

Bullish confirmation starts developing.

Above $70:

RiskOn momentum setup.

Above $75:

Potential trend reversal becomes much more convincing.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚠️ IMPORTANT DISTINCTION

My conviction in the COMPANY is currently higher than my conviction in the CHART.

AST keeps doing many of the things long-term bulls wanted:

✅ Technology validated
✅ Bigger satellites deployed
✅ Manufacturing scaling
✅ Carrier partnerships expanding
✅ Government opportunity developing
✅ Contracted revenue growing
✅ Commercial network getting closer

But the market already assigned ASTS a massive valuation (~$23B market cap).

That's why execution matters so much from here.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 RISK/REWARD

🐻 Bear Case:

Launch/manufacturing delays + slower commercialization + valuation compression.

$40-50 is absolutely possible.

🐂 Base Bull Case:

Deployment continues, commercial revenue accelerates and the market increasingly values AST as telecom infrastructure rather than speculative space tech.

I'd look for a re-rate toward the $75-100 zone.

🚀 Full RiskOn / Execution Bull Case:

Constellation scales successfully, carrier monetization works, government revenue expands and AST proves meaningful subscriber economics.

At that point, debating whether ASTS is worth $60 or $80 becomes irrelevant.

The debate shifts from whether the tech works to how big the infrastructure business could get.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

MY TAKE:

$ASTS is still one of the asymmetric growth names I follow closest.

But asymmetric doesn't mean low risk.

The technology is becoming increasingly validated.

The business model is becoming increasingly validated.

The constellation is increasingly real.

Now AST has to prove the ECONOMICS.

That's the next stage of the thesis.

Long-term thesis: constructive 🟢

Short-term technicals: Neutral/Bearish 🟡

RiskOn potential: Extremely High 🔥

I'd get more constructive on a sustained reclaim of $65-$70.

Until then I'm respecting the chart.

$ASTS

Position: long $ASTS calls.

text:
Same Four Rockets, Same Clock, Different Day

Sunday offered less a news cycle than a loop confirmation: the SDA Tranche 1 Falcon 9 launch, Nuri's NeonSat-2 through 6, the unlabeled Long March 12 payload, and another Starlink batch all cleared pads again at 9:36 PM — the identical timestamp @NASASpaceflight flagged just one day earlier, which either means the schedule has genuinely stabilized or nobody's updating the slot anymore. SpaceflightNow ran live coverage regardless. The SMILE first-light story and the Spolzino lunar-gaps feature, both freshly minted in Saturday's and Sunday's briefs respectively, reappeared in today's feed as well, suggesting NASA's own channels are still catching up to news the trade press already filed. The one item with actual new substance was NASA's Curiosity team logging sols 5022 through 5028 at Cache Creek — modest, workmanlike, and notably not a rerun — while Ars Technica wandered off-topic again with an Egyptian "retainer sacrifice" forensics piece, continuing its pattern of supplying reading material rather than space news.

Community energy split along now-familiar lines: Starship's Flight 16 prep kept generating the same cautious, schedule-skeptical chatter as Ship 43 reportedly works through Mega Bay 2 toward a possible Florida move and 39A launch, Europe's post-ISS crew-and-station ambitions drew another round of measured optimism shadowed by funding doubts, and SMILE's first images continued earning quiet, genuine credit as the week's one unambiguous win. IAC 2026 added a new wrinkle, pulling the community's attention toward conference photo-ops and insider banter rather than anything resembling hard news. At this point the feed has gotten so good at tracking its own repetition that it's started to feel less like a newsletter and more like a logbook of how long four stories can be rebroadcast before someone finally asks if the launch pad has a new booking system or just a broken clock.

Washington offered Saudi Arabia a nuclear deal on terms it never gave the UAE.

Riyadh was offered enrichment on Saudi soil without the IAEA Additional Protocol. In 2009, the UAE accepted a ban on domestic enrichment as the price of American reactors, and that standard has now been set aside for its largest neighbor.

The offer came months after the United States struck Iran's nuclear program, a campaign that destroyed centrifuge halls and underground complexes. Iran still retained enough 60% enriched uranium for more than ten warheads if further enriched, and it struck every Gulf state in retaliation.

The United States maintains bases and defense agreements across the Gulf, and none includes a nuclear guarantee. Allies in Asia and Europe have a formal umbrella to argue over, while Gulf partners have never been offered one.

Turkey is the one state in the region with American nuclear bombs on its soil. They remain under American control, and Erdogan has asked publicly why Turkey cannot have its own. Ankara has since begun commissioning the Russian-built Akkuyu plant and launched a submarine program that opens a legal pathway to domestic enrichment.

text:
Eritrea Is Selling the Coast, Not Opening the Country

Verified: Eritrea suddenly owns a hotter piece of the map.

Its roughly 1,000-kilometer Red Sea coastline is becoming more valuable as war threatens shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and near Yemen. Washington has removed sanctions imposed over Eritrea’s role in the Tigray war, saying the move serves U.S. regional interests. Eritrean officials are now talking trade, investment and opportunity.

What they are not talking about is opening Eritrea.

The country has held no national election since independence. Independent media was shut down in 2001. Teenagers still pass through military training before entering mandatory national service that can stretch indefinitely. The United Nations counts more than 679,000 Eritrean refugees and asylum seekers abroad, though Eritrea disputes both the number and the explanation behind it.

The geography changed.

The government didn’t.

Why it matters: Repression gets priced differently when you own something powerful countries suddenly need.

Eritrea can offer coastline, ports, minerals and strategic access without surrendering control over its citizens’ labor, movement, information or political power.

That is the transaction worth watching.

The outside world isn’t necessarily rewarding reform.

It may simply be paying more for the real estate.

text:
Just imagine. You are out getting a late-night snack with friends — pizza. You finish and pay. As you step out onto the street, you see carnage. Nine people shot. 

You rush away, but the scene stays with you.

Over the next few days, the story emerges.

Now imagine this was not the shooter's first offense. Two years earlier, he had shot at a carwash employee who approached him to ask him to stop loitering, because the way he was brandishing his gun was driving customers away.

Instead of complying, the shooter raised his gun at the employee. He shot at him, but missed.

In court, District Attorney Laura Conover decided not to seek prison time. Instead, she offered the shooter a plea deal and recommended probation.

"She just has a different philosophy," a previous prosecutor said. "To me, he goes to prison."

Conover mocked him in response. "I guess he hasn't found any joy in retirement," she laughed. 

The judge was hesitant, but followed Conover's recommendation.

"I'm going to give you another shot," he told the defendant.

Some shot. More like nine. Nine people gunned down on the street, in front of the place you and your friends went out for pizza.

It might have been you. It should have been prevented.

Does Conover find "joy" in that?

Finally, imagine, in your city of Tucson, Arizona, the local government is throwing its whole weight behind an effort to euthanize a dog — a livestock guardian dog — who made a single, isolated mistake and bit a family member while under duress, trying to keep his home and animals safe against coyotes.

text:
GalaxEye – Space Imaging Opportunity

Space-tech startup GalaxEye is using its proprietary SAR + optical imaging technology to build higher-resolution Earth-observation satellites, with plans to scale into a major commercial satellite constellation.

Key takeaways

US patent: GalaxEye recently received a US patent for its core SAR technology, which combines optical images with Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). SAR enables imaging even through clouds and the atmosphere, addressing a key limitation of conventional optical satellites.

The patent covers the company's architecture and system used to align and synchronise optical and microwave sensors, enabling simultaneous, spatially and temporally matched data acquisition.

Technology differentiation: The company says the patent is a foundational element for building larger satellites, with ambitions to scale to a ~30-satellite constellation.

Commercialisation progress

GalaxEye became the first Indian startup to put an OptoSAR satellite into space aboard a SpaceX rocket.

Its satellite Mission Drishti was launched in May and is currently in the commissioning phase.

During commissioning, the satellite is being tested through activities including solar-storm monitoring, image calibration and system validation before commercial operations.

Management expects commercialisation after the commissioning process, which takes a few months, and says the satellite had already achieved ~85% of its objectives.

Large addressable market

The global commercial Earth-imaging market was valued at around $6.55 billion in 2024 and is projected to more than triple to ~$21 billion by 2033, according to SkyQuest Research.

GalaxEye's technology targets sectors including defence, agriculture, infrastructure, insurance, maritime intelligence and disaster management.

The company has already attracted customers globally, with clients in ~80 countries, indicating potential demand beyond India.

Funding & scale-up
GalaxEye has raised $21 million to date.

It plans to launch two new satellites within the next two years, with the next-generation satellites expected to be larger and offer higher resolution.

The key thesis is the combination of optical + SAR imaging in a single satellite architecture, potentially providing all-weather, higher-quality Earth observation compared with conventional optical-only systems.

The major milestones to watch are successful commercialisation of Mission Drishti, customer conversion, satellite deployment cadence, resolution/data quality, constellation scale-up and additional funding requirements.

The US patent strengthens the technology/IP proposition, while the planned constellation could allow GalaxEye to transition from a technology demonstrator into a scaled commercial Earth-observation platform.

The Q4 Alpha Playbook: Navigating the Upcoming TGE Wave and Mainnet Launches

Fellow traders, as we step into October, the market is presenting us with a dense schedule of token generation events (TGEs), mainnet launches, and product releases. In this liquidity-driven environment, staying ahead of supply shocks and fundamental catalysts is the difference between getting chopped and capturing the move.

Let’s break down the upcoming calendar (October 5, 2026, onwards) and how to position ourselves.

1. The Immediate Horizon (Early October)
We kick off with immediate supply events. PNT (Oct 5) and WHUF (Oct 8) are set for token releases. Historically, early-month unlocks face thinner liquidity as market makers rebalance. Unless there is a massive narrative tailwind, I expect these to face short-term sell pressure. For traders, this often creates a "buy the dip" scenario post-unlock if the project fundamentals are solid.

2. The Mid-Month Tech Catalyst
The real narrative shift happens mid-month. SO (Oct 19) and FHENIX (Oct 21) are both scheduled for Mainnet releases. This is crucial. Mainnet launches transition a project from speculation to utility. Keep a close eye on FHENIX specifically—mainnet launches often trigger volatility spikes 48 hours prior as speculators front-run the news. AERO (Oct 21) also has a product release, which could reignite interest in the DEX narrative if the update offers tangible yield improvements.

3. The Late-October Unlock Cluster
The end of October is heavy. RITUAL, PULT, ALLOX, and RSGP all have token releases scheduled. This cluster suggests a broad market supply increase. Smart money will likely rotate out of these assets leading up to the unlock, looking for strength elsewhere.

4. The Q4 Wildcard
Looking further out, the list is dominated by Q4 "Token Releases." INFI, JUMP, APYX, STRATO, TOWN, TENEO, CT, VAR, and EXT are all on the docket.

· The Strategy: Do not blindly short these. With Q4 being historically bullish for crypto, these unlocks might be absorbed by retail FOMO. However, the "Token Release" label implies inflationary pressure. I will be watching the funding rates on perpetual futures for these assets. If funding goes deeply negative pre-unlock, it indicates a crowded short trade (potential squeeze). If it stays neutral, expect a slow bleed.

Trader’s Bottom Line:

· Avoid catching falling knives on the Oct 5 and Oct 8 releases unless you see high-volume absorption.
· Play the Mainnet narrative (SO, FHENIX) for short-term momentum trades.
· Watch the order books for the Q4 list. Good projects often see a "sell the news" event on unlock day, followed by a bottoming structure 3-5 days later.

Manage your risk, size down during high-volatility unlock windows, and remember: in a bull market, unlocks are liquidity events, not just bearish events.

text:
Story time: 
I don’t think I’ve told you all my origin story (how I got into tech). My dream skill wasn't UI/UX or graphic design, it was always video editing. Not because I was attracted to it but because I wanted it for my YouTube channel. 

In 2019 and 2020, I was a diehard gamer. 
Best SF3 Player in Nigeria for 3 consecutive months by Nekki. But I had one restraint: my videos couldn’t compete on an international level because of edit quality, etc. 

Don’t get me wrong. I was still pulling thousands of views on YouTube; I wasn’t creating on any other platform aside from YouTube. 

So I sought to get access to a laptop or PC I can use to learn video editing. Then I discovered Edobits, where every student gets assigned their personal computer for the entire cohort. 

But video editing was one of the last design skills to be taught. I had to learn graphic design first, then branding and then UI/UX, but I’ve already gathered enough knowledge to navigate the editing software on my own. 

In 2021 school resumed, and I didn't join them for the editing classes. But I needed my personal computer to continue my YouTube and gaming dreams. So I offered my design skills to make some money. 

I landed my first gig in November 2021 as a designer, and in 2022 I did a book/brochure design for the Edo state government as a contracted designer. Then late 2022 I got to work as an Edojobs designer for the Edo State Govt with zero qualifications. I didn’t even show an SSCE certificate 😂

The rest is history, and I ended up pausing my YouTube dreams, doubling down on tech, and never offering my video editing skills as a service. 

Fast forward to 2026 in this AI wave; it’s been my 2nd most lucrative skill after @framer developements that is, so I guess you can call me a video editor. 
It's weird how things turned out. 😂 

So I would leave you with this: no matter how little you can learn of a skill, learn it. You don’t know if that would be the skill to put food on your table at a certain point in your career. an

As always, live your life with purpose and positivity. Have a great week ahead of you.

text:
2 commercial property managers (EXACT ICP) asked for a snow removal onsite walkthrough within 3 days of cold email going live, for a local landscaping client

small utah operator, 5 towns, campaign went live sep 30. first quote request oct 2, walkthrough invite oct 3

confident we can get it to a sustainable 3-5 qualified on-site walkthroughs every week

which means minimum 12 a month, 144 a year, with even 10% close rate on qualified ones it'd be 14 contracts signed

and you know commercial landscaping & snow removal deals are massive 

how:

1. the list is only properties she WANT to actually service. ~2,450 tier 1 commercial accounts mapped in her area, kept the ones that control their own grounds and fit her crew size. 

322 people across 4 segments for round 1

2. split by who controls the lot: local property managers, out-of-area managers with a property in her towns, owner-run lots (dealerships, warehouses, storage, hotels), assisted living. different campaigns for each as messaging changes dramatically

3. the email asks about their lot: "who's plowing the lot on State St this winter?" then one offer. 15 min walk before the first storm, one price for the whole season, and a plan for where the snow goes so you don't lose spots

4. the PS assumes they already have someone: "if you've already got someone you like, no worries, the number's still yours to compare against." one of the 2 plows his own lot and wanted backup for big storms

text:
3 years back I took the biggest risk of my life.

I left a high paying tech job at Amazon to write on the internet.

What happened next changed my life.                                                                                                                                

Lets start from the beginning. I had never used X. I didnt have an audience. I had no clue how I could monetise my writing, skills or experience. I just wanted to build a business doing work I love and live a life of freedom and purpose.

The first few weeks were tough. Going through beginner hell, posting into the void and barely seeing any growth. But I continued to show up and eventually things started getting better. I learned the basics of digital writing, found my voice and started understanding the X game.

It has not always been easy but I have made decent progress since then:

- Gained 10,000 followers on X
- My business has crossed $200K+ in profit
- Have worked with 60+ high ticket clients around the world
- Have generated $500K+ in results and built a portfolio of case studies
- Multiple clients have crossed the $5K/mo and $10K/mo mark
- Some of them even quit their jobs to build full time
- Scaled a private community to $40K

But numbers only tell half the story. The real reward has been the lifestyle. I get to do work I love everyday. I only work with people I like. I can go to the gym whenever I want. I have plenty of time to read books or go on long walks. I can take a vacation without asking anyone for permission. I have control over my time and schedule. And that was a big part of the vision when I quit my job to build online.

The best part is you dont need anything revolutionary to get here. All you need is a small but quality audience, an offer that solves a painful problem and a predictable way to turn traffic into leads and clients. You dont need to go viral, have a massive audience or hustle 12 hours per day to build a 6-figure internet business.

I am writing this post for one simple reason. To help you if you are in the same position I was in 3 years back. Having real skills and experience. Knowing your potential. Knowing that you are meant for something more. But feeling stuck and not knowing how to start.

I hope my story gives you permission to start. You dont even need to quit your job. You just need to publish your ideas online, talk to your audience and solve a painful problem. I am a regular guy. If I can figure it out so can you.

If you want to do it faster shoot me a DM and lets chat.

text:
In 2001, China had 1.15 million college graduates. The class of 2026 is projected at 12.7 million. Over 25 years, that’s an 11-fold increase. And it’s completely changed the underlying logic of “job hunting.”

What was it like for the class of 2001? The initial employment rate for undergraduates from universities directly under the Ministry of Education was 92.08%, and 93.8% for postgrads. College grads were a scarce resource back then. Companies literally fought over students on campus. The guaranteed job assignment system had just ended—you’d drop your résumé at a job fair, have a decent chat, and you were hired. Jobs were expanding, and people were in short supply.

What’s it like for 2026? 12.7 million new grads, plus those from previous years still unemployed, returning overseas students, and people who failed the grad school or civil service exams. The total job-seeking pool has long since passed 15 million. Meanwhile, campus recruiting growth is nowhere near keeping pace. In July 2026, the national surveyed urban unemployment rate was 5.2%—not high at first glance—but the structural problems are all concentrated on young people. The process has changed too: scrolling job apps, mass applying, AI screening, personality tests, online info sessions, multiple rounds of group interviews, AI video interviews, background checks… a single job search can drag on for months.

I dug up an old book, *Absolute Workplace Challenges*, published around 2003. There’s a passage that still feels completely relevant today: Employers have vacancies but always complain they can’t find the right people; college grads complain they can’t find jobs; and some employers at job fairs put up signs saying “No new graduates.” The author’s question back then was—what kind of talent do employers actually need, and where’s the gap between that and what graduates offer?

The fact that this question was asked in 2003 shows it’s not a new problem. It’s structural. A mismatch that already existed twenty years ago, now amplified 11 times by sheer scale, has become what we see today.

There’s a book called *Learning from Japan: A Survival Guide for the Era of Decline*, which thoroughly examines Japan’s lost two decades. The first chapter is titled “Decisions Under the Unemployment Wave: Protect Jobs or Protect Development.” It makes a point: employment isn’t an isolated livelihood metric. It and industrial upgrading are two ends of a scale that have to be balanced with the same pot of money. Back then, Japan protected jobs too aggressively, and ended up preserving outdated capacity and inefficient positions along with them. People didn’t lose their jobs, but their incomes stagnated for ages. We need to see this clearly, not just fixate on that decimal point in the unemployment rate.

Then there’s “degree inflation.” A master’s becoming the default isn’t simply because there are more master’s grads. It’s that job requirements for competency have been raised, and people’s degrees have been pushed up even faster in response. The fastest-shrinking demand is for roles that can be replaced by tools—admin, customer service, basic clerical work.

Years ago, I made a half-joking remark: Can’t get into a good school, can’t find a good job, can’t afford nice clothes… when you’re complaining about how unfair life is, maybe take a look at stock market wipeouts and mortgages that never seem to end. That wasn’t telling people to accept their fate. It was telling people to first take a clear-eyed look at the cards in their own hand. For the hand dealt in 2026, the most valuable card isn’t a diploma. It’s “being able to solve problems others can’t.”

It used to be “people looking for jobs.” Now it’s “jobs looking for people.” Whoever can turn their skills into tags an algorithm can recognize gets seen first. On this point, the class of 2001 and the class of 2026 ultimately have to accept the same reality.

I expect that 12.7 million figure will edge up a bit more next year. Rather than discussing the “toughest job-hunting season” every single year, we’d be better off first aligning the two charts—academic programs and industry demand. That’s the real source of that 11-fold gap.

As for employment, that’s just how it is in China. Huge population. Expanding enrollment diluted the value of degrees. The original intention was good, but it produced a lot of low-quality talent. Of course, from a dialectical perspective, we also have to acknowledge the success of higher education reform, because the base of high-quality talent has also expanded. The total number of skilled people in society has grown, solving many scientific and technical problems that couldn’t be solved before.

In short, this cohort of graduates still has it really tough. Those with skills need to show what makes them different. As for classmates who just coasted through school… well, they can just keep coasting through life.

text:
If your peace depends on the daily news cycle, you will live in perpetual exhaustion.

Over the past week, the headlines felt like a masterclass in global volatility: the United States quietly ended its 23-year military presence in Iraq, G7 nations scrambled to release 100 million barrels of emergency fuel reserves to combat shipping crises, central banks pushed interest rates to multi-year highs, and across France, over 735 schools shut down as more than 2,000 young people were arrested in violent street riots (Wikipedia Current Events).

To the secular mind, the world looks like a ship with a broken rudder spinning into chaos. But when you examine these exact events through the unchanging lens of Scripture, you are reminded of a grounding, timeless truth: Not a single headline from this past week caught the Sovereign Creator by surprise.

Here is what shook the world over the past seven days—and why our focus belongs firmly on the King of Kings.

1. The 23-Year Chapter Closes in Iraq & The Fragility of Man-Made Peace
On September 30, American troops completed their final withdrawal from Iraq, marking the formal conclusion of a 23-year military footprint that began in 2003 and spanned multiple generations of service members. Simultaneously, shipping choke points in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea triggered emergency defense talks, while an attempted mid-air hijacking aboard Flydubai Flight 1073 was narrowly averted over Saudi airspace (Wikipedia Current Events).

Think about that timeline for a moment: 23 years, trillions of taxpayer dollars, thousands of lives sacrificed, and countless political promises made. Yet the Middle East remains just as fragile, contested, and volatile today as it was when the first boots hit the sand.

Why? Because human treaties and military force can enforce temporary ceasefires, but they can never heal the human heart.

Christ told us plainly in Matthew 24:6:

"And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for this must take place, but the end is not yet."

Notice what Jesus commands: "See that you are not alarmed." He did not say conflicts were trivial, nor did He call us to be callous to innocent lives caught in war zones. He commanded us not to panic.

Empires spend trillions posturing on the world stage, but Psalm 20:7 reminds us of where real security lies:

"Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the Lord our God."

Politicians, generals, and treaties will always fail to deliver ultimate peace. Pray for our soldiers returning home, pray for families living under the shadow of conflict, and rest in the truth that God alone establishes and removes rulers according to His sovereign will (Daniel 2:21).

2. G7 Fuel Reserves, Interest Rate Hikes, and the Idol of Financial Security
On Friday, October 2, the G7 nations jointly announced a plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from strategic stockpiles to fight skyrocketing energy prices caused by regional conflicts. Across the globe, central banks—such as the Reserve Bank of Australia raising its benchmark rate to 4.60%—continue tightening credit to battle persistent inflation that refuses to die (Wikipedia Current Events).

Working families feel these high-level macro moves every single week at the gas pump, the utility bill, and the grocery checkout.

When global markets shake, it exposes a spiritual reality that modern culture works overtime to ignore: Money is a terrible god, and wealth is a shifting shadow.

Our grandfathers lived through the rationing of World War II and the stagflation of the 1970s. They didn’t obsess over speculative market apps on their phones; they budgeted carefully, lived well below their means, eliminated debt, and relied on honest labor and God's daily provision.

Scripture provides an unvarnished warning in Proverbs 11:28:

"Whoever trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like a green leaf."

If economic headlines are keeping you awake at night, let this season be an intentional call to simplify. Steward your resources faithfully, cut consumer waste, work hard with your hands, and anchor your confidence in Christ’s promise in Matthew 6:31–33:

"Therefore do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?'... For your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you."

3. French Youth Riots & The Crisis of Fatherless Despair
Over the past five days, cities across France—including Paris, Marseille, and Nantes—were rocked by mass student rioting, leading to over 735 closed secondary schools, hundreds of injuries, and more than 2,000 arrests (Wikipedia Current Events). Closer to home, senseless violence shattered a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, leaving dozens wounded.

Pundits on television blame school funding, class sizes, or political agitation. But when you look deeper, you see a generation of young people starving for purpose, moral direction, and fatherhood.

When a society systematically removes God from public life, mocks traditional family structures, and tells young men that their masculinity is toxic, it creates a spiritual vacuum. Without a transcendent anchor, youth inevitably drift into cynicism, rage, and destructive nihilism.

King Solomon diagnosed this millennia ago in Proverbs 29:18:

"Where there is no prophetic vision the people cast off restraint, but blessed is he who keeps the law."

This is why mentoring young men and building strong, Christ-centered homes is not merely a lifestyle preference—it is cultural and spiritual warfare. If fathers do not disciple their sons in duty, discipline, and humility, the street and the digital algorithm will gladly do it for them.

4. The Shift: Moving From Panic to Purpose
Christian men and women were never promised an easy, tranquil world. In fact, throughout church history, God specifically placed His people into dark, turbulent, and morally confused generations so that the light of the Gospel would shine with unmistakable clarity.

When the culture around you is panicking, an unshakeable, calm Christian man is a living sermon. When everyone else is terrified of the future, a family grounded in prayer shows the world what real hope looks like.

Here is your charge for the week ahead:

Lead your home spiritually: Turn off the 24-hour news commentary. Open your Bible at the dinner table, look your wife and children in the eyes, and pray over your household.

Be the steady anchor at work: In your shop, warehouse, or job site, refuse to participate in the water-cooler culture of fear, complaining, and political rage. Be the calm voice of wisdom and diligence.

Steward your local community: You cannot control what happens in foreign straits or central bank boardrooms, but you can control how you treat the neighbor down your street, how you serve your local church, and how faithfully you manage your own budget.

Rest in the Unshakeable Kingdom: Nations will rise and fall. Global reserves will deplete. Leaders will pass away. But the Lord God Almighty sits enthroned over the flood forever (Psalm 29:10).

"Therefore let us be grateful for receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, and thus let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe." — Hebrews 12:28

Step into this week with your boots laced, your hands ready to work, your family protected, and your eyes fixed on Christ.

text:
Grass-fed beef, in Britain. The next shelf along will be bottled rain.

Two thirds of the farmland on this island cannot grow a crop. It is too wet, too steep or too high, so it grows grass, which it grows better than anywhere on earth, and then it grows some more, because it is still raining.

Wales gets 150 wet days a year. The grass has never once stopped. Neither have the cows. A Welsh cow has never been offered an alternative to grass in her life, and would not know what to do with one.

Nobody built a feedlot here because nobody needed one. The field is the feedlot. The rain is the feed lorry. The bill is nil.

Then a label arrives from America, where the alternative to grass is a pen in Kansas with 50,000 animals in it, and it gets stuck on a cow that was standing in a bog in Cumbria with nowhere else to be.

The premium is 40%. The certification body has a logo. The supermarket has a shelf for the sticker, and a shelf next to it for the beef that came off the same hill without the admin.

Grass-fed, in Britain, is a label for a country that is drowning in the thing the label promises. It is the Sahara selling certified sand.

Keep an eye out for the sequels. Water-fed trout. Air-breathed chicken. Gravity-finished eggs. Sheep, reared outdoors, in weather, at a premium, with a leaf on the pack.

The cow has been eating grass on this island for 4,000 years without a certificate.

The sticker has been here 20, and it is the only part of the arrangement that has ever needed a marketing budget.

text:
6 things I check before any client signs for a car:

1 - The invoice price

Not the sticker, not the "market price",  but not the final word either. 

On a car in high demand, like a Lexus GX, invoice barely matters since you're not getting it below MSRP no matter what.

2 - Current manufacturer rebates

These change monthly and dealers don't volunteer them.

Some models have thousands sitting on the table that never make it into the conversation.

3 - The doc fee by state

Some North Carolina dealers charge close to $900. New York dealers legally can't charge more than $175. 

That gap alone can make sourcing out of state worth it.

4 - The F&I menu

The issue was never that it's hard to read. 

It's that everything gets priced in ways that make it hard to tell where the value is. 

Never accept the first price offered on any line item, because knocking a few thousand off a marked-up warranty is still a real win.

5 - The Carfax, even on "like new" cars

A 2025 model with 1,400 miles priced $20,000 under market isn't always luck. 

Sometimes it's a lemon law buyback wearing a low price tag and buybacks are only generally supposed to be repaired before resale, which doesn't guarantee much.

6 - The out-the-door number, in writing

No surprises, no new line items, no renegotiating something you already agreed to.

Run all 6 and there's nothing left for anyone to hide.

The past two weeks have been another big learning curve for me.

I thought that with the help of our current app and systems, I could finally handle client tasks, monitoring, and execution on my own. But then I got sick for more than two weeks, and shortly after, my wife got sick too.

That was a real wake-up call.

We realized that no matter how good our systems and tools are, we simply can’t handle everything ourselves. There needs to be a team behind the system.

And now, I’m really excited to share some great news.

I’ve onboarded an Email Specialist! 🎉

They will be handling all email-related concerns, especially email setup, configuration, deliverability, and monitoring.

Lately, we’ve also been receiving feedback that some emails are landing in spam. Interestingly, based on the data we’re seeing, everything appears to be working normally. This made us realize that there may be changes or updates in email platforms and deliverability that we need to stay on top of.

Having an Email Specialist means we can now properly configure each email account, monitor deliverability, troubleshoot issues, and make adjustments whenever platforms introduce new updates.

And we’re not stopping there.

We’re also almost ready to onboard a Social Media Manager and Video Editor who will help our clients manage their social media accounts, build and grow their personal brands, and consistently create and edit content.

This is a big step for us.

The goal is not just to have more people on the team. It’s to build a system where every part of our clients’ businesses is properly supported by someone who specializes in it.

We’re slowly moving from “I have to do everything” to “we have a team that can handle it.”

And honestly, that feels like one of the biggest milestones we’ve reached so far. 🚀

Still learning. Still improving. Still building.
But we’re getting there.

Of course, the goal is the same. Higher service offer x same service rate.

text:
I got really good at SEO and honestly it made me lazy.

Traffic was NEVER a problem.

If I wanted more money I could create more pages, rank for more stuff, make more offers and send more traffic at them.

So email was kinda alien to me.

I knew we should probably be doing more with it but why bother learning a whole new thing when I could just get another 100k people to the site? 😂

Then traffic bombed.

And suddenly we were in trouble.

Because what I'd never really appreciated was we were basically selling to the tiny % of people who landed on the site at the exact moment they wanted to buy.

Everyone else just... left.

So I had to get good at email.

And that was the first big unlock for me.

Because now I didn't need someone to be ready TODAY.

I could get them onto an email list when they first became interested.

Before they needed our solution.
When they were researching.
When they knew they wanted something but weren't sure what yet.
Or when they were just at a completely different stage of consideration.

Cool.

But then I had another problem...

How the hell do you move someone from reading an email to actually BUYING something? 😂

So I learned that.

Then I wanted to sell bigger ticket things.

Which gave me another problem.

Now people weren't gonna click a button and casually drop $10k-$30k.

So we needed webinars.
Sales calls.
Applications.
Closers.
Follow up.
Blah blah blah.

So I learned how to sell that way.

Then after a while I got tired of THAT too 😂

I didn't want a sale to require a webinar or some 90 minute sales call every time.

So I started wondering how expensive a thing I could sell just using email and a Google Doc.

Turns out... pretty expensive.

So I got good at that.

Then I started wondering why I needed the fucking Google Doc 😂

So I learned how to sell bigger and bigger ticket things without that too.

Just emails.
Conversations.
Offers.

Then eventually I ran into another problem...

I got tired of delivering the products and services 😂

And that's pretty much how I accidentally ended up with the business model I have now.

I find people with big email lists who LOVE delivering what they do...
but don't particularly love the sales and marketing bit.

And I take that bit off their plate.

Figure out what we can sell.
Create the offer.
Write the emails.
Handle the conversations.
Make the sales.

Then I usually take 30-50% of the revenue we create.

Which is kinda funny when I think about it.

I didn't wake up and decide...
"I'm going to become an email marketer."

Every time I solved a problem I just found the next constraint 😂

First I learned how to get attention.
Then how to keep it.
Then how to sell to it.
Then how to sell more expensive stuff.
Then how to remove the calls.
Then how to remove the funnel.
Then eventually...
how to remove myself from delivering the bloody thing.

So now I basically sit in the bit between...

"You've got a load of people who trust you."

and...

"Let's find something they really want to buy."

Turns out that bit can be worth quite a lot of money 😂

The door was sealed to the dying. Compassion opened it. Neglect kept it open.

Canada removed the requirement that death be reasonably foreseeable. Track 2 now covers people with disabilities who are not dying. Disability is a Charter-protected ground under section 15. Offering death as the reliable service, while the supports required to live remain chronically underfunded, does not fulfill that protection. It narrows it.

In 2024 Track 2 recipients were far more likely to self-identify as disabled, and Ontario coroner data shows they disproportionately come from poorer neighbourhoods with unstable housing. Supports that might relieve the suffering are offered in a minority of cases. MAID is funded and timely. Disability income often is not.

Poverty is not an eligibility criterion. Once disability qualifies someone, the suffering produced by missing supports can be treated as reason enough. Autonomy requires alternatives. When death is the reliable service and living is not, the choice is no longer clean.

Canada abolished the death penalty in 1976 because the state taking a life raised a moral question it would no longer answer with a rope. The question did not retire. It returned as a medical procedure, with cost savings attached and the paperwork arranged so the intervention disappears. Ontario instructs providers to record only the underlying illness or disability and to make no reference to MAID or the drugs on the medical certificate of death. Manner of death is to be certified natural where that option exists. A state that administers the death does not require the death certificate to say so. The savings stay quiet because the record does.

text:
Number of times Palestine could have been “free” = 10.

Number of times Palestine accepted “liberation” = 0

Major proposals offering a path to Arab/Palestinian statehood in former Mandate Palestine (or later the West Bank and Gaza):
•1937 Peel Commission: British plan for a small Jewish state and larger Arab state (linked to Transjordan). Jews accepted the principle; Arab leadership rejected any Jewish state.
•1947 UN Partition (Res. 181): Jewish state (~55%, much desert), Arab state (~45%), international Jerusalem. Jewish Agency accepted; Arab leaders and states rejected it and went to war. No Arab state formed; Jordan took the West Bank, Egypt Gaza.
•1948–1967: Jordan and Egypt controlled those areas and did not create a Palestinian state. Post-1967 Khartoum Resolution: no peace, recognition, or negotiations with Israel.
•1978 Camp David: Autonomy framework for West Bank/Gaza tied to Egypt–Israel peace. Egypt accepted; PLO rejected.
•1993–95 Oslo Accords: Mutual recognition, Palestinian Authority interim rule, and timetable toward final-status talks on a state. Process stalled amid violence, settlements, and unmet conditions.
•2000 Camp David / Clinton Parameters: Palestinian state on ~94–96% of the West Bank plus swaps (near-equivalent area), all of Gaza, Arab neighborhoods of Jerusalem, limited refugee options mainly to the new state, non-militarized status. Barak accepted parameters as a basis; Arafat did not agree. Second Intifada followed. Taba 2001 narrowed gaps but produced no deal.
•2002 Arab Peace Initiative: Full withdrawal to 1967 lines, Palestinian state with East Jerusalem capital, agreed refugee solution, in return for Arab normalization. Israel did not accept the terms as stated.
•2003 Road Map: Quartet phased plan to a provisional then final Palestinian state. Not implemented.
•2008 Olmert offer: ~93–94% of West Bank plus 1:1 swaps (near full area), all Gaza, link between them, shared Jerusalem arrangements, symbolic refugee numbers into Israel. Abbas did not accept or formally respond.
•2013–14 Kerry talks and 2020 Trump plan: Frameworks based on 1967 lines with swaps (Kerry) or a smaller demilitarized state with economic aid and conditions (Trump). Both collapsed or were rejected; core disputes remained borders, Jerusalem, refugees, security, and recognition.
No proposal produced an agreed, implemented Palestinian state.

If there’s care to be correct…

First, this is interesting: 

1939: 40 million Arabs in the world.
2026: 450 million Arabs in the world
1939: 17 million Jews in the world.
2026: 16 million Jews in the world
1939: 4 sovereign Arab states
2026: 22 sovereign Arab states
1939: 0 sovereign Jewish states.
2026: 1 sovereign Jewish state

And, your analogy doesn’t describe what happened.  It treats Israel as a neighbor who bought an adjacent plot, then seized your land and ordered you out under an Old Testament claim, with resistance redefined as terrorism.  You’re collapsing several different things into one story.

There was no sovereign Palestinian state to seize. From 1517 to 1917 the land was Ottoman imperial territory, administered as districts of Syria and Beirut, not an independent Arab polity. After the Ottoman collapse, the League of Nations Mandate for Palestine (1922) assigned the territory to Britain and explicitly recognized the historical connection of the Jewish people with Palestine and the grounds for reconstituting a Jewish national home, while protecting the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities. 

The 1947 UN partition plan proposed two states. 

👉🏼The Jewish leadership accepted it. 
👉🏼The Arab leadership rejected it and went to war.

Land purchase was not a claim on someone else’s country.  Late Ottoman and Mandate-era Jewish buyers acquired tracts from willing sellers, often absentee landlords. 

That is ordinary property transfer. 

Sovereignty came later, from the Mandate framework, the partition resolution, and the 1948 declaration after the Arab rejection of partition AND not from a title deed plus a Bible verse.

The 1948 war was an invasion, not an eviction.  Israel declared independence inside the partition lines.  Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Iraq, and Lebanon invaded.  Jordan then held the West Bank and Egypt held Gaza until 1967; neither created a Palestinian state. 

The refugee flows of 1948 came out of that war (flight, expulsions in combat zones, and in some places instructions from Arab leadership to leave).

NOT EXACTLY, “I bought next door, now pack up.”

The “you must leave” line is false as policy.  Arab citizens of Israel are about a fifth of the population, with citizenship, voting rights, and Knesset seats. 

The live dispute is over the West Bank and Gaza and, for Hamas and rejectionist factions, over Jewish sovereignty anywhere west of the Jordan. 

Camp David 2000 and the Olmert offer in 2008 were rejected.  

Gaza was vacated in 2005 and became a launchpad, not a state.

“Terrorist” is not a label for ordinary border defense.  Suicide bombings, rocket fire on cities, the October 7 massacre, and hostage-taking are aimed at civilians and at the existence of the state, not at a property dispute.  Ottoman rule was not a quiet idyll either:  Jews lived as dhimmis, and communal violence long predated 1948. 

Competing nationalisms after the empire fell are what produced the modern conflict.

The neighbor-buys-your-land sketch swaps the legal and military record for a morality play.

Replicating the Ankara Formula: Somalia’s Attempt to Bilateralize the Somaliland-Israel Crisis

Somalia is waving for relations with Israel, as it used to do for Ethiopian access to the sea in 2024, in the middle of the crisis.

This could not be missed, and it’s clear: the same tactic from the same dude, thinking the case is the same and will have the same result.

Somalian president Hassan indicates the possibility of normal relations with Israel in the future  the third official indication of such on the world stage.

He appears to be attempting to bilateralize the dispute and replicate the Ankara Declaration model, effectively substituting direct engagement with Israel for the Somaliland dimension

👉🏾In 2024, in the middle of the Ethiopia-Somalia crisis over the MoU with Somaliland, the Somalian president clearly and repeatedly indicated that he was not opposed to Ethiopian access to a sea route through Ethiopia, rather than the Somaliland part being involved.

He meant to discuss the offer directly with Ethiopia and remove Somaliland from the equation, which resulted in the Ankara Declaration, where he granted Ethiopia its right to access the sea.

👉🏾In 2026, in the middle of his struggle and crisis with Somaliland-Israeli recognition, again he is clearly and repeatedly first through other officials and now by himself indicating a normal relationship with Israel as a state-to-state relationship if the Somaliland involvement part is solved in his way.

Very important to notice: he repeatedly talks about Israel’s approach in this way, which he means through Somaliland.

He is doing the same old tactic: approach Israel, replace Somaliland, and make a deal similar to the Ankara Declaration.

Worth noting, the question was not about his view or plan regarding a relationship with Israel. It was straightforward:

“Aren’t you concerned that Somalia and Somaliland could become an arena for conflict and competition between, for example, Turkey and Israel  between regional powers?”

But he chose to emphasize this part, which is not even directly in line with the question:

“Perhaps we could have a relationship with it at some point in the future, but it will not be an alternative to Turkey, and it cannot be compared with Turkey.”

A wave to Israel and a guarantee to Turkey to calm it down.

Ignoring the fact that Somaliland and Israel have officially recognized each other and established their respective embassies, and thinking it is just like the Ethiopia case, tells a lot about Hassan Sheikh’s capacity and ability to assess the situation.

Insanity is doing the same thing and expecting a different result.

Again, this means Somalia’s position on Somaliland-Israeli relations was not grounded in the moral principles and religious rhetoric that Hassan himself initially invoked.
