text:
Cheap technology is getting surprisingly good — but the best bargains usually have one thing in common: they keep things simple.

A recent test of 24 low-cost gadgets bought for under $250 showed how much the budget-tech market has changed. Some extremely cheap products worked far better than expected, including a programmable mini keypad, decorative lighting and simple accessories built from mature, inexpensive components.

But the results changed quickly when products required more complicated engineering.

A roughly $10 robot vacuum looked the part but lacked the suction, navigation and cleaning hardware needed to perform like a real autonomous cleaner. Cheap smart glasses also offered some useful features, but compromises in sound privacy and functionality made their limitations much more obvious.

Then some products cross the line from inexpensive into misleading. One USB drive advertised as 16TB appeared to offer more than 15TB when connected to a computer, but deeper testing found only about 57.9GB of usable storage. That is not a compromise — it is a fake specification that can eventually put users’ files at risk.

Safety deserves even more caution. Cheap chargers, batteries and electrical devices may work perfectly during a quick test while hiding weaknesses in components or protection systems that are much harder for buyers to evaluate.

The lesson is not that cheap tech should be avoided. In many categories, inexpensive products are better than ever. The smartest bargains are usually products doing one simple job well, without making extraordinary promises.

text:
A reporter told Steve Jobs that America had gotten out of service. Jobs answered in one line: "You don't need service if you're not innovating."

If you are still selling what you sold five years ago, maybe you do not need much help at the counter. Apple was not doing that. Half the Macs in the stores were going to people who had never owned one. Windows customers, almost 50 percent.

The first two stores opened five years earlier, one in California and one in Virginia. By the Fifth Avenue opening there were 147. Genius Bars. A 32-foot glass cube over a store the landlord had offered underground. Jobs called that idea crazy, then called back a day later and asked for the cube.

He did not talk about the brand. He said a brand is trust, and trust works like a bank account. A great iPod is a deposit. A bad experience is a withdrawal. People who spend the day worrying about the brand instead of the product usually do not get what they want.

I don't think he was defending retail. He was saying service only matters if the thing you are selling keeps changing.

Still wild that the store everyone said America did not want became the one that switched half its customers off Windows.

Was the cube the product, or was the product the reason anyone walked down into it?

text:
Every line in this list about RFK Jr. is a real event. Here is each one with its date and its paperwork.

The dinosaur bones. Kennedy says he flew on Epstein's jet twice in the 1990s, both times with his family. Easter 1993 to Palm Beach to see his mother, after Ghislaine Maxwell, a friend of his wife Mary through a food-allergy charity, offered the seats; Epstein's limousine took the family from the airport by way of his house, where they waited for another car. A year or two later it was Rapid City, South Dakota, with Mary and four of the kids, for a weekend of fossil hunting on the Pine Ridge Reservation. He put this on Fox News himself in December 2023. Maxwell told the Justice Department in July 2025 that "we went dinosaur bone hunting in the Dakotas" and that she never saw anything improper from him. The files released in February 2026 added a 2012 email in which she asks Epstein, "didn't we go fossil hunting with him and Bobby Kennedy in N Dakota?" His name is in Epstein's contact book. That is the whole documented Epstein record: two flights, a house stop, a fossil weekend, thirty years ago.

The barn. Mary Richardson Kennedy was found hanged in an outbuilding at the family's Bedford, New York home on May 16, 2012, two years into a divorce that had cost her custody of their four children. The Westchester medical examiner ruled it a suicide; the toxicology found three antidepressants and no alcohol. The report also recorded that the fingers of both hands were between the rope and her neck, with an abrasion. The examiner gave two readings, a last struggle or a hand still placing the rope, and did not choose between them. Her sister told Kennedy at the scene, "you have killed my sister." The Richardsons hired investigators and then dropped a planned wrongful-death suit. The same day, Eva Dubin emailed Epstein that Mary had been found dead. He wrote back one word: "whoops."

The grave. Kennedy beat Mary's brother in court for the right to bury her, chose the Kennedy ground beside Eunice and Sargent Shriver in Centerville, Massachusetts, and buried her on May 19. In early July, seven weeks later rather than days, he had the coffin dug up and moved about 700 feet to an open section near the gate where the family was negotiating to buy 50 plots. The Barnstable town clerk said no disinterment permit was ever filed; Massachusetts requires one even for a move inside the same cemetery. The Richardsons' lawyer said the family had not been told.

The bear. On October 6, 2014 a dead bear cub turned up under a bicycle beside a Central Park path, and the state necropsy said high-speed collision. The mystery lasted ten years, until the New Yorker's fact-checker called. On August 4, 2024 Kennedy posted a video of himself telling Roseanne Barr that a woman's van had killed the cub in front of him on his way to go falconing, that he put it in his own van to skin and eat, ran out of time, and left it in the park with an old bike so it would read as a cycling accident. "My prints were all over that bike." The statute of limitations was one year.

The raccoon. Isabel Vincent's 2026 biography printed his diary for November 11, 2001: "I was standing in front of my parked car on I-684 cutting the penis out of a road-killed raccoon, thinking about how weird some of my family members have turned out to be. My kids waited patiently in the car." He told People he kept such parts to study later. He is a licensed master falconer and wildlife rehabilitator who studies animal skulls and skeletons; his daughter once described him chainsawing the head off a beached whale and bungee-cording it to the minivan roof for the drive home. Asked about the raccoon by TMZ this April, the Secretary of Health and Human Services laughed and his security walked him away.

None of this is a secret. All of it sits in a medical examiner's file, a probate fight, a town clerk's statement, a DOJ transcript and his own video. What sits in none of it is a finding that Mary's death was anything other than what the examiner ruled.

text:
Three Ships, One Sea: Size and Speed Decide the Bitcoin Treasury Race, but the Storm Decides Who Finishes

Recently there have been lots of discussions around the fastest horse in the bitcoin treasury race. With respect to the horses, I think we are at the wrong venue. A racetrack is flat, dry and fair. The rail is painted, the distance is posted, and nobody drowns.

Bitcoin is none of those things.

So grab a coffee and come down to the harbour. Stand on the quay and look out. That water is bitcoin: wide, deep and moody. Some mornings it lies flat as glass and every captain looks like a genius. Some nights it turns black, the wind starts to howl, and it tries to climb into the boat with you. There is no forecast worth trusting. There never has been.

Now look at the ships. Every one of them is full of people. The passengers and crew are the shareholders, and they bought their tickets on trust. They do not steer. They cannot see the charts. They are counting on one person in a peaked cap, up on the bridge.

That person is the captain, and the captain has two jobs. The first is to make headway, because a ship that never leaves port is just an expensive building. The second is to bring everyone home alive. On a calm day those two jobs get along fine. In a storm they start to fight.

Three ships are out today. One is enormous. One is ridiculously fast. One is still being built while it sails. I will not tell you their names. You will work it out.

How sailors judge a ship

At the end of the quay there is a bar where the old sailors sit. They have watched ships come and go for longer than they will admit. Ask them how to judge one and they hold up two fingers, usually before the first drink is finished.

First finger: how big is it?

On this sea, size means one thing: how much bitcoin is in the hold. A big hull carries more people and has more to offer on board. It laughs at waves that would flip a dinghy, and it crosses water that smaller boats do not dare to enter. The price is agility. A giant turns about as quickly as a shopping mall, and by the time it has finished turning, the reason for turning may have passed.

Second finger: how fast is it?

Speed here has nothing to do with the price of bitcoin. The sea sets that, and it rises and falls under every ship alike. Speed is how quickly the bitcoin behind each passenger's ticket is growing. The companies call it BTC yield. A small boat can leap forward on a splash of fuel. A giant has to burn a mountain of it to gain a single knot, which is why the biggest ship is rarely the quickest.
Size and speed. Those are the two numbers the crowd on the quay shouts about.
Then the old sailors go quiet, and one of them usually adds a third question. Nobody asks it on a sunny day. Everybody asks it when the sky goes dark.

Does it float?

The cruise ship

You see this one before you see anything else.
At first you take it for a headland. Then it moves. A white wall of steel slides across the horizon, so big that the other boats look like bath toys beside it. Gather every other ship in the race into one harbour, weigh them together, and this one still outweighs the lot.

It was the first to sail these waters, back when the old sailors said it could not be done. It has been through storms that had the whole harbour holding its breath. That is how it conquered the sea. Not by being quick. By being out there, voyage after voyage, getting bigger.

Life on board is very comfortable. There is a deck for every kind of passenger: thrill seekers up top, cautious savers down below, and something in between for everybody else. The buffet never closes. The gangway is wide enough for the largest institutions on earth to stroll aboard without turning sideways. No other ship can host them. No other ship has the room.

Speed is another matter. Nothing this large does anything quickly. It has settled into a stately cruise, and the small boats now pass it without much effort. A change of course is announced a week before it happens. Even a repair takes a season. The crew spent part of this year below deck, reinforcing the hull plate by plate.

Now the part that should make the small boats nervous. Down in the engine room there is far more power than the captain ever uses. Everybody on the water knows it. If he pushed the throttle to the stop, the wake would rise like a hill and send every small boat in the race spinning like a rubber duck.

He does not touch it.

He stands at the rail instead, hands behind his back, watching the little ones dart about below. He is not racing them. He is waiting for them. His dream is to look across the water one day and see more cruise ships sailing beside him, and you cannot grow a fleet by sinking it.

The sports boat

You hear this one before you see it.

A snarl from somewhere past the harbour wall. Heads turn on the quay. Then it comes round the point in a sheet of spray, small, loud and low to the water. Fresh paint. Spotless deck. Not a scratch on it. And bolted into the back, an engine that clearly belongs on a much bigger boat.

It is the fastest thing out here, and it knows it. While the cruise ship glides along in its stately way, the sports boat runs laps around it. Actual laps. Each time it flashes past, the crowd on the quay goes wild. It is the newest boat with the newest engine, and for its size nothing on the water comes close. It is the crowd favourite, and it is not shy about it.

You would think the captain would be satisfied. He is not. He wants more.

So he went through the boat and threw every spare kilo overboard. Anything that could ever drag on the hull is gone. I suspect the cup holders went too. What is left is engine, fuel and nerve.

Then he did something the crowd did not expect. He bolted a survival kit to the stern. Flares, rations, a raft, a radio. It will not ride out a storm forever. It will keep every soul on board alive for a long time, long enough for rescue to arrive.

Ask him about it and he gives you his logic, and it is hard to argue with over a drink. If a tsunami comes, it takes everyone: the big ship, the little ship, the lot. So he will not crawl around the ocean being afraid of it. For anything smaller, he has the kit.

Then he grins, turns the key, and the throttle goes flat to the floor.

The old sailors watch him go and say nothing. They have seen fast boats before. Some of those boats became legends. The sailors do not say what became of the others.

The electric boat

The third ship is the odd one.

From a distance it looks like someone walked away in the middle of building it. Scaffolding up one side. Cables everywhere. Engineers pacing the deck with clipboards. And from somewhere deep in the hull, a faint hum that nobody will explain.

The crowd on the quay has opinions about this boat. Some of them laugh.

Do not laugh at the scaffolding. Look at the hull. It is already bigger than the sports boat's, built wide and deep, as if somebody were planning for a far larger ship than the one you see. And below deck, behind a sealed door, sits an engine unlike anything else in the race. It was designed by two crews from opposite shores, who do not usually share a workshop. By all accounts they are very pleased with themselves. Nobody outside has seen the drawings.

There is one small problem. Nobody has been allowed to switch it on.

New machinery has to be proven before it goes to sea, and that means the harbour inspectors. They come aboard. They open panels. They test, they frown, they write things down. Inspectors do not hurry for anyone, least of all for an impatient crowd.

So in the meantime the crew has put up a temporary sail. It is an honest, old-fashioned thing on a very modern boat. When the wind blows, the boat moves. When the wind drops, the crew stands around looking at the canvas. That is why the sports boat keeps vanishing over the horizon while the electric boat is still clearing the harbour mouth.

Go up to the bridge, though, and you will not find a worried man. The captain is calm in the way people are calm when they know something you do not. He is only temporarily behind, he says. The day the inspectors sign the last page, he takes down the sail, opens the sealed door and goes full speed ahead. He is not trying to catch the sports boat. He means to become the next cruise ship.

And the others cannot follow him there, he believes. They can admire the engine. They can photograph it from the quay. They cannot simply copy it.

Until then, he waits for the signature and watches the wind.

So who wins?
The crowd wants a simple answer. The sea does not have one. Each captain is sailing a different race, and each has placed a different bet.

The cruise ship is betting on size. Its captain believes that scale wins in the end, and that a sea full of big ships is better for everyone than a sea with only one. Watch whether it can keep gaining ground as it keeps growing, because every knot is harder to find than the last.

The sports boat is betting on speed. Its captain believes the best answer to a dangerous sea is to cross it quickly, with a survival kit on board for the bad days. Watch the kit. The harder the engine runs, the more that kit has to hold.

The electric boat is betting on an engine nobody has heard run. Its captain believes that once it starts, nobody catches him. Watch the inspectors. Until the last page is signed, the boat is a promise and a sail.

On a calm morning you can make a case for any of them, and on the quay people do, loudly.

Then the weather changes.

It always starts the same way. The light goes flat. The gulls head inland. The flags that were hanging limp begin to crack. The crowd stops arguing about speed, and for the first time all day everyone is looking at the same thing: the horizon.

The sea does not care who the crowd was cheering for. Calm days reward speed. Storms reward whatever keeps you afloat: the weight of the hull, the kit on the stern, the engine that either starts or does not. Nobody knows which of those holds until the water tests it.

So before you buy a ticket, walk the dock and ask the old sailors' three questions. How big is the ship? How fast is the bitcoin behind each ticket growing? And what happens on board when the weather turns?

Then pick the ship you can sleep on.

One last thing. I never did name the ships. Tell me in the replies which is which.

Hope you all enjoyed this piece. Thank you for reading. 🧡😊

text:
Lawyers who were given top-of-the-range cars last week by the late controversial tycoon Wicknell Chivayo - Wilson Manase and Sylvester Hashiti - in his last act of "generosity" or "philanthropy" will not be able to legally collect the vehicles today as directed given that everything under his estate is now frozen until the executor is appointed.
Upon death, a deceased person's estate and bank accounts are legally frozen, and no one can withdraw funds or deal with assets without permission from the Master of the High Court.
Under Zimbabwean law, no one has the legal authority to buy, sell, distribute or deal with any assets of a deceased estate until an executor is formally appointed and granted Letters of Administration by the Master of the High Court.
Chivayo offered Manase a brand 2026 Lexus GX 550 valued at US$220 000 and US$250 000 for "fuel and personal upkeep", saying he was "reserving the best for the last".
Chivayo called Manase about it to find out about the offer acceptance.
He also gave Hashiti a brand new 2026 Range Rover Sport Autobiography as well as US$250 000 for fuel and upkeep; his fourth car donation to him having previously given him three other vehicles.
In what proved to be his final act of giving before he died in a helicopter crash near Marondera last Wednesday, Chivayo, having distributed cars and cash worth multiple millions in the past three years under a secret state project, Chivayo said to Manase:
"Please go and see VICTOR on MONDAY next week and collect your 2026 LEXUS GX 550 valued at 220 thousand USD, fully paid for and ready for your collection. In addition, please collect some small petty cash of US$250,000 CASH for your fuel, personal upkeep.
As for my other younger brother Advocate Sylvester Hashiti , I know i have bought you 3 cars before but I checked and realised there's no law that restricts wealthy clients from spoiling their lawyers again so surely there's no harm in you getting a fourth one. Please accompany Mr Wilson Manase and also collect your brand new 2026 RANGE ROVER SPORT AUTOBIOGRAPHY as well as 250 thousand USD in cash for FUEL and upkeep."
Giving lawyers expensive cars and huge amounts of has raised eyebrows amid indications that was a state patronage operation.
Commenting on the what legally happens in such situations, Advocate Thabani Mpofu said:
"The legal position is relatively straightforward. Upon a person’s death, their proprietary interests devolve to the estate and may be administered only by the duly appointed executor or executrix. Similarly, contractual obligations owed by the deceased cannot be discharged until an executor or executrix has been appointed. 
It is for the executor to assess the deceased’s claims and liabilities, determine which claims should be honoured, and pursue any claims to which the deceased may have been entitled.
Accordingly, if property not yet delivered by the deceased is distributed or disposed of before the appointment of an executor or executrix, that conduct would constitute a criminal offence and will expose those responsible to prosecution."
Advocate Lewis Uriri declined a recent public US$350 000 gift package from Chivayo, despite having accepted similar tokens of appreciation during earlier professional engagements in 2024.
After Uriri publicly declined the new offer, Chivayo respected the decision, emphasising that their long-standing mutual respect remains.
Chivayo said Manase was his main lawyer who introduced him to Uriri and Hashiti, "so my appreciation would be incomplete without recognising the man himself who was always there from the beginning". 
Chivayo said:
"WE COME A VERY LONG WAY and i have known him literally since 1998, when I was still renting ONE ROOM in Hillside and trying to find my feet in life. 
He has watched my journey from those humble beginnings to where I am today. Through the years, he has been much more than just my lawyer but has been a FATHER FIGURE, MENTOR, BROTHER, ADVISER and trusted confidant."

text:
The @CFTC just proposed its first crypto market structure rules: Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) & Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM)

tl;dr The CFTC is building what it can w the authority it already has now that the Clarity Act seems unlikely 

Highlights from @ChairmanSelig WSJ op-ed this morning:

– Covers crypto the CFTC & SEC already agreed are non-securities in their joint interpretation earlier this year (eg bitcoin & ether)

– Sets requirements for CFTC-registered exchanges that list those assets

– It's opt-in. Nothing forces spot crypto onto CFTC venues (Selig concedes that one takes Congress)

– The carrot: these venues could offer retail customers margined, leveraged or financed trading. State-licensed exchanges can't

That last point is the big one IMO. Retail leverage is the one product a state money-transmitter license can never get you, and the CFTC is betting it's enough to pull exchanges into a single federal scheme voluntarily

Also a pretty pointed Gensler callback: the "come in and register" era is over & exchanges no longer have to concede their listings are securities to get a federal home

As @MichaelSelig says himself: agency rules can't substitute for a statute forever, and a future Commission can unwind this. But it's a real federal on-ramp, which is more than we had yesterday

text:
🚨How to Destroy an Empire in Two Years or Less!
Trump edition...

I wrote this. Economics, technology, and history are my ground; geopolitics is not. I normally start alone, from a blank page. This time I kept an artificial intelligence in the room longer than usual, because my own was not enough for the alliance mechanics. The darkness and the argument are mine. Anyhow unlike others I am transparent and I thought I come clean with the fact that three Super Intelligent tools helped with this production! So any errors: blame AI!

Empires rarely die in a blaze. They die when the people who used to pretend the arrangement was mutual stop pretending. The American version rested on three things that were never as solid as the brochures: the title of leader of the free world, the alliances and soft power that made the title look earned, and the petrodollar plumbing that turned oil into a standing order for Treasuries. Two years is an optimistic schedule. The current administration appears to be treating it as a personal best.

Start with the title. “Leader of the free world” was always a marketing phrase with a military attached. It worked because enough governments found it cheaper to nod along than to build the alternative. The performance review is now being written by people who have already updated their résumés. In a 2025 Ipsos survey across 30 countries, Canada ranked as the country most expected to have a positive influence on world affairs, while America’s positive reputation had dropped 13 points in a year to 46 percent. A 2026 Pew survey found majorities in every European country polled lacking confidence in Trump on world affairs, often by three-quarters or more. A Politico poll had German respondents scoring “the US protects democracy” at 1.8 out of 10, France at 2.1, Canada at 2.5. The free world, it turns out, is allowed to notice when the leader starts invoicing the congregation.

Canada is the cleanest exhibit. Early in the second term the pitch was absorption: the 51st state, delivered with the usual mix of tariff and taunt. Ottawa declined the merger. By September 2026 the European Commission was offering Canada associate membership instead — trade, critical minerals, the Arctic, defense-industrial integration — and Prime Minister Mark Carney was in the European Parliament treating it as a feature, not a hostage note. Canada had already become the first non-European country inside the EU’s SAFE joint-procurement instrument. A Canada-EU summit is set for late October in Montreal. Trump called the associate-member idea potentially hostile and threatened heavy tariffs on Europe if he decided the intention was bad. Carney’s line, stripped of diplomat gauze, was that middle powers either sit at the table or end up on the menu. Forty years of continental integration does not unwind because a speech got spicy. It frays when the senior partner keeps demonstrating that the contract is optional.

Ukraine supplied the sequel in miniature. Washington spent recent weeks asking Kyiv to stop hitting Russian oil refineries, on the grounds that the drones were doing unpleasant things to global diesel prices. Ukraine hit the Kuibyshev refinery in Samara the day after one such appeal, kept striking into early October, and had Zelensky explain, in English and without visible remorse, that attacks on Ukrainian energy would be answered on Russian refiners — the things that fund the war. A private call reportedly fixated on “diesel, diesel, diesel.” Kyiv’s counter-offer was a mutual energy ceasefire. Moscow did not take it. The client read the patron’s request, checked the war, and continued the war. That is not rebellion in the romantic sense. It is what happens when the security guarantee has been marked down and the recipient still has drones.

Europe’s finger is less theatrical and more procedural, which is how Europe does contempt. The July 2025 Turnberry deal — 15 percent U.S. tariffs on most EU goods, European industrial tariffs dropped, large aspirational promises on energy purchases and investment — was the ceasefire. By early October 2026 EU lawmakers had frozen the ratification vote after replacement U.S. tariff orders pushed duties through the agreed ceiling. Paris floated the anti-coercion instrument. Separate tariff threats tied to Greenland produced emergency meetings and talk of a dangerous downward spiral between allies. U.S. military aid authorized for Ukraine had, on one accounting, collapsed from above $19 billion in 2024 toward a few hundred million for 2026, with Europe moving into the primary-financier seat whether it felt ready or not. None of this is a European army materializing overnight. It is the moment the dependents stop assuming the invoice will be paid in the old currency of deference.

The petrodollar is the part everyone oversells, including the funeral directors. Oil is still overwhelmingly invoiced in dollars; the non-dollar share of crude trade is still a minority. Dollar reserves remain near 57 percent of the global total. Saudi-China oil settlements in yuan have risen sharply in some tallies, Russia-China energy trade has shifted, and the old story in which Gulf surpluses automatically recycle into Treasuries is already dated — several producers are borrowers now, not the world’s bankers. The system is eroding at the edges and being argued over in public. It has not been abolished by tweet. An empire that needs the plumbing can still kick it. An empire that also alienates the customers makes the kicking louder than it needs to be.

What replaces the old arrangement is not a single heroic successor. It is a set of workarounds. Canada and the EU talking about integrated defense industries and critical-mineral stockpiles. Middle powers announcing that reliability is now a competitive market. European officials saying, in public, that the continent may have to defend itself from Washington as well as from the usual suspects. Polls in which Canada outranks the United States as a positive influence, and in which Europeans rate American democratic leadership somewhere between a shrug and a malpractice suit. None of these actors has the carrier groups. Several of them have concluded they would rather pay for redundancy than rent the old brand.

The dark joke is that this is efficient. Soft power, alliances, and dollar primacy were the cheap way to run the empire: other people did part of the work because the brand still paid them. Burn the brand, invoice the allies, and instruct the client state to stop shooting at the refineries because the pump price is politically awkward, and the cheap method ends. What remains is the expensive method — hard power, bilateral deals, and the hope that nobody important builds a habit of routing around you. Two years is fast. It is not magic. It is mostly the decision to stop maintaining the story that made the cheaper empire possible, delivered with the confidence of a man who thinks the story was a favor he was doing them.

text:
While my US Host Family’s father was a millionaire and the family had 5 beautiful vacation properties (2 at the ocean, 2 at the mountains and one at the lake), their own house was a mess, that was cluttered with stuff they haven’t used for years, and 4 boys were sharing one small bedroom. The oldest 10-year-old boy had a separate bed in the shape of racing car. The 6- and 8-year-old were sleeping in a bunk bed, and 4-year-old had no own bed. He was either sleeping with his parents or with his oldest brother in a racing car bed. 
My Host Father kept promising my Host Mother he would buy them a new house that suited better their family size for years, and she kept waiting.
Kids had soccer trainings and games after school almost every day, including at least on day on weekends. They all hated soccer. It was their father’s choice. He believed it was prestigious for his children to play soccer. 
My Host Family were also members of a local golf club and were paying high annual membership costs. My Host Father never played golf during 1.5 years I stayed with them. We used that expensive membership a few times coming with my Host Mother and kids for brunches without the Host Father. That way their pricey membership was at least somehow used. 
My Host Father used sunroom by the pool as his unused office. It was cluttered with mountains of documents that were never used. My Host Mother wanted that room to be used by kids as a transition room before entering the pool. So, when my Host Father went away to hunt for a week, she organized a cleanup: together, we cleared the clutter out of that room and threw away items covered in a thick layer of dust that had accumulated over the years. Of course, My Host Mother got into a big trouble when my Host Father returned home. Kids started having friends coming over to swim at the pool. They used the sunroom to change, have snacks and drinks.
My Host Father went hunting for rabbits once a year to Nebraska. To do that he kept a separate vehicle, Ford Expedition, and 10 beagle dogs. Dogs were kept outside in large fenced cages. Kids were responsible for cleaning dog poop daily after school before soccer practices. Sometimes my Host Mother could do it, and I was also helping kids clean while also supervising them. My Host Mother and I were also buying 50 pound dog food bags and dumping them into plastic containers for boys to use it to feed the dogs. 
Kids could not have normal holidays from school and enjoy their childhood in full, because they were forced to clean that dog poop even during holidays. I felt sorry for them. During one of their spring holidays, I decided to let them have a break and enjoy holidays like all children do, and I did it for them that week. Plus, it turned out to be easier for me to do it myself than organize 4 boyz do it.😁
Also, my Host Father organized a chicken coop, and kids had to clean that as well, and collect eggs. Those kids had no childhood and no peaceful moments to themselves. Almost every moment of their day was taken by some chores. They were not happy kids like other kids, who were enjoying their childhood.
One day a friend of my Host Mother came by and brought a cute black and white dog, told it was found on the street, and offered my Host Mother to adopt it. Kids fell in love with the dog, as it was kind and wasn’t barking non-stop like beagles. At first, my Host Father said No to keeping the dog, then he agreed with condition that it would be kept outside in the cage. Kids still were very happy.
My Host Father’s Day was not as busy as he organized for his kids. Usually he had peaceful mornings, watched news and did some trading in front of the screens, then went to his office around noon and returned in a few hours.⤵️

text:
Want to know how we can save The Town of East Greenwich?  

Local Control, Land Use, & EG’s Missed Opportunities

By Donna Costantino and Peter Rodgers

In 2023, Rhode Island enacted sweeping changes to housing and land-use laws, reshaping the rules municipalities must navigate when planning for growth and reviewing development proposals. The changes affected comprehensive permits, zoning, subdivision and land-development review, inclusionary zoning and Comprehensive Plans, all while state law required municipalities to update and re-adopt those plans every 10 years with a minimum 20-year planning horizon.

East Greenwich was not caught by surprise: development pressure was on the doorstep, and town officials were participating in statewide discussions. Our community had additional options beyond waiting to see what the State House would do. The EG Town Council could have studied the proposed legislation, adopted resolutions expressing the Town’s concerns, worked with other municipalities to advocate for local control, testified before the General Assembly, and made sure East Greenwich’s own Comprehensive Plan was updated before it expired.

The town had warning

The state’s push to change the rules was already underway years before the major legislation was enacted in 2023.

In 2021, the RI House created a special commission to study land use, development, housing and regulation, with the goal of recommending changes to promote growth and address the state’s housing shortage. By 2022, the Rhode Island League of Cities and Towns was actively discussing housing and land-use legislation and its potential impact on municipalities. East Greenwich’s Town Manager was involved in that statewide municipal organization, serving on its executive board.

In 2022, Town Council candidate Peter Rodgers proposed that the Town Council write a resolution pushing back against state overreach, “in which they urge [legislators] to offer input in the language of the law and to vote in support of our town’s interest. This would send a proactive message to our state representative and senator about whether we support a bill that could negatively affect us. Ideally, before a law is passed, they should provide our lawmakers with specific ways in which they would like the law amended.”

Since the 2023 General Assembly session, more than 60 bills have been enacted affecting municipal authority and the rules governing housing, land use, and development.

Other towns voiced concerns early; East Greenwich waited

Other municipalities took steps to protect local control while the EG Town Council waited to act, despite previous warnings. In early 2023, before the housing legislation was passed, Exeter, Hopkinton, and Warren adopted resolutions in support of local control. They argued that housing and development decisions should remain with individual municipalities.

On June 26, 2023, following a summary of enacted legislation by the Town Solicitor, the EG Town Council asked questions for the first time regarding impacts on EG and how much local control still remained with the town.

In spring of 2026, 13 other Rhode Island communities adopted resolutions addressing concerns over the State’s affordable-housing laws and their impact on municipal authority. East Greenwich eventually acted as well, adopting Resolution 2026.09, in support of the legislation that would allow affordable units to be counted when building permits are issued rather than waiting for certificates of occupancy.

While we commend the council for writing this resolution, we believe it should have acted sooner, and the resolution, while positive, stopped short of asking the State to address the broader challenges facing municipalities as they accommodate additional housing.

Comprehensive Plan expiration and its consequences

While many Rhode Island municipalities also lagged on comprehensive plan updates (the process is multi-year, costly, and resource-intensive, and recent state law changes complicated timelines), East Greenwich’s delay carried particular consequences.

The expiration of East Greenwich’s Comprehensive Plan was not unforeseeable. The town knew for 10 years when its 2014 plan would expire, yet formal work on a replacement did not begin in earnest until nearly two years after the 2024 deadline. East Greenwich was not waiting for development pressure to arrive. It was already here.

The clearest example was the 410-unit Division Road proposal, the largest residential development in the town’s history. The proposal had been before the Planning Board since 2020, with public hearings continuing through 2023. The project was planned in a rural part of town without sewer connections or public transportation. By 2022, residents were raising concerns about putting a large-scale residential development on what is, in practical terms, a rural road with limited infrastructure.

The Division Road project also exposed a limitation in the town’s existing land-use framework. The developer was able to utilize a Comprehensive Permit to bypass the normal local approval process because the 2014 Comprehensive Plan had designated the Northwest quadrant for high-density housing.

To the current Town Council’s credit, it appealed the decision and negotiated an important modification with the developer: 50 percent of the 410 units will be age-restricted to residents 55 and older. That agreement helped address some of the project’s potential impacts, particularly peak-hour traffic and the demand for municipal services, while preserving the 25 percent affordable-housing component.

Division Road also presented a broader lesson for the town. Residents had made clear their concerns about the scale of development in this rural area, underscoring the importance of revisiting the Town’s land-use policies before additional proposals reached the approval process. Instead, another proposal soon followed.

Ridgeline Estates, a 43-unit development, entered formal review in July 2024, just months after the Comprehensive Plan expired. It was approved by the Planning Board in March 2025. The decision raised concerns for neighboring residents about possible cumulative effects on property values and has already impacted Faith Hill Farm, a valuable adjacent community resource which provides equine assisted therapy to people in need.

Then, in March 2026, nearly two years after the 2014 Comprehensive Plan had expired, the Town Council ultimately adopted a new plan through Ordinance No. 932. The adoption was an important step, but significant development decisions had already been made. The question is not whether adopting a new plan was worthwhile but why the Town did not complete it sooner, before the previous plan expired and while major development proposals were already advancing.

The Council’s subsequent action is particularly significant. In June 2026, the Town Council amended its Comprehensive Plan submission to the State through Ordinance No. 933, removing provisions relating to the creation of zoning in the Northwest quadrant, the same area previously designated for housing development. If the Town could reconsider its approach to the Northwest quadrant in 2026, why couldn’t it have begun that conversation before additional development proposals moved through the approval process?

We also applaud the Council for expanding its Land Trust properties in recent years to protect open spaces for residents to enjoy. These efforts are important, but land acquisition alone cannot substitute for a comprehensive land-use strategy.

The state’s Division of Statewide Planning continues to list East Greenwich’s 2014 plan as “Expired,” as the town waits for the June 8 plan submittal to be approved by the state. The plan remains in effect locally, but the state is no longer bound by it for state-level actions until the plan is approved.

Meanwhile, farms and large parcels of land remain for sale in the northwestern quadrant of town. Until the updated plan receives state approval, those properties remain an important concern for residents who want to preserve the rural character of this part of East Greenwich and avoid another round of large-scale development proposals under the existing framework.

What the Town Council should consider now

We believe the Town Council should monitor an important concern at the state level regarding the pace and scale of development and the potential impact on our natural resources.

The Rhode Island General Assembly has established a Special Legislative Commission to Study and Provide Recommendations on Water Supply Planning for New Housing Developments in Rural Communities. The commission was created to examine how new housing development can affect the safety, quality, and capacity of public water supplies and watersheds in rural communities.

According to Scott Millar, formerly of RIDEM, drinking-water resources, aquifers, wetlands, flood-prone areas, prime farmland, forests, and unique habitats need protection because environmental damage can be difficult or impossible to reverse. He also argues that existing state environmental protections are insufficient, particularly for farms, forests, and habitats. Therefore, municipal land-use authority is essential so local governments can determine where and at what density housing should be built while protecting drinking water and important natural resources.

Affordable Housing: Where and how?

There should be no confusion about the goal: East Greenwich needs more affordable housing and we support this statewide initiative. As of 2025, East Greenwich had approximately 8.29 percent of its housing stock designated as deed-restricted affordable housing, which is very close to meeting the 10 percent state goal.

Donna and Peter, who is a member of the Affordable Housing Commission, believe that the town should guide development towards utilizing existing properties close to transportation, shopping, medical care, and jobs. Rather than clear-cutting forests, renovating and repurposing existing structures can provide housing while preserving open space and making better use of infrastructure that is already in place. The town can also help preserve existing housing stock through the use of “offsets.” In this scenario, developers rehabilitate rundown structures which bring down property values in neighborhoods, turning them into quality, deed-restricted affordable homes.

Responsible growth is about more than meeting a housing target; it means considering where development occurs, whether infrastructure can support it, and whether its scale and design fit the surrounding community.

Our promise for the future

If elected, we will take a proactive approach to housing, meet planning deadlines, and work to protect East Greenwich’s rural and historic character. We will testify on behalf of our community at the state level, work with state representatives to amend laws that impact East Greenwich, and coordinate with other rural communities that share similar concerns. And, to ensure that our town is staying on top of legislative issues, we plan to create a legislative commission to monitor and examine proposed legislation impacting our town before it is too late and it becomes law.

As candidates for East Greenwich Town Council, Peter and Donna bring decades of leadership and management experience. Peter’s more than 30 years as a submarine officer and program manager, combined with Donna’s 34 years in Rhode Island state government leadership, provide proven experience leading teams, managing complex projects, and responsibly overseeing public resources and taxpayer dollars.

text:
Turkish bases are thinning Kurdistan's border woodland, satellite data show, but far less than claimed

Videos of trucks carrying timber to Turkish military bases have sparked a major controversy in Iraq's Kurdistan Region in recent days, over whether Turkey is systematically cutting the region's border forests.

The issue has gone viral across Kurdish media. Rudaw, Kurdistan24 and opposition outlets each offer a different version of events, each fitting its own agenda.

To test the claims independently, The National Context analysed 25 years of satellite imagery covering every district of the Kurdistan Region. Satellite data is the most independent way to check what is happening on the ground. Here is what the findings show:

Woodland in areas of Turkish military activity, especially Amedi district in Duhok province, is being lost at about twice the rate of comparable woodland elsewhere. The loss is modest in scale, however, and concentrated where Turkey has built networks of new roads and outposts, including cleared hilltops consistent with helicopter landing sites.

Each year's loss is small. But it recurs every year and falls on the region's highest oak woodland, so the cumulative damage is significant enough to cause concern.

The long-term record shows no collapse of the region's forests. It does show a slow decline in the border belt relative to the rest of the region. The border belt is defined here as the woodland within 25 km of Turkey in Amedi, Zakho and Mergasur - all mapped. That pattern points to loss in specific patches.

Sentinel-2 satellite imagery shows where those patches are. Between 2017/18 and 2024/25, 5.6% of Amedi's woodland showed a marked drop in greenness, the highest share of any district. Zakho followed at 4.8% and Mergasur at 3.8%. Elsewhere the share was 2.8% in Akre, 2.5% in Soran, 2.1% in Penjwen on the Iranian border, 2.0% in Duhok and 1.7% in Pshdar, also on the Iranian border.

Several indicators contradict the opposition's allegation that the cutting is systematic and commercial, feeding furniture production inside Turkey:

Commercial logging usually spreads across any forest that trucks can reach. The border belt doesn't fit that pattern. If you split its woodland into 1 km squares, nearly 90% of the loss is packed into just one in ten squares, and about four in five squares show no loss at all.

Moreover, the loss follows the newly built roads. In the Metina mountains, a main target of Turkey's 2021 operation, 29% of woodland within 250 m of a new road showed a marked drop, against about 10% further away. The losses came in 2023 and 2024, the years a switchback road and then a ridge-crest road were built.

More importantly, the scale is limited. Across the border belt, about 36 km² of roughly 1,300 km² of woodland has shown a marked drop since 2017. About 20 km² of that is more than comparable woodland lost elsewhere, and 12 km² of the extra loss is in Amedi. That is 0.34% to 0.5% of the belt's woodland a year. By comparison, woodland in the region without Turkish military activity loses about 0.2% a year, Iran's Zagros oak forests about 0.16%, and forests worldwide about 0.25% - that is gross loss.

Also for context, other war zones have suffered far heavier losses. Syria's coastal forests lost 24% of their cover between 2010 and 2020, and western Syria 19% between 2010 and 2019. More than half of Afrin's forest cover was reported lost within about three years of Turkey's takeover. On Ukraine's front lines, 5% to 16% of forest was damaged in a single season.

The figures also strongly contradict any timber trade. Assume every affected hectare were dense, mature woodland at the top of published estimates, about 76 tonnes per hectare. The extra loss would then yield at most about 20,000 tonnes of wood a year, and all of the marked drop about 35,000 tonnes. Real yields are likely far lower. Moreover, most of this woodland is scrub oak, cut back repeatedly over generations. It is firewood grade and of little use to furniture makers. 

Even the theoretical maximum would be about a 0.1% of Turkey's annual industrial wood harvest. Small-scale sales, such as surplus firewood sold in Sirnak or Hakkari or the felling of individual walnut and plane trees, cannot be ruled out, but a trade on the scale alleged can.

text:
In a flash of green, she fades out of sight. It could only be her, given the embarrassing show she put on for the school. Harry locks his eyes where he last saw her and stands from his seat on the steps of the stairs leading out of the ballroom.

“Hey Ron, I think that’s enough of the Yule Ball for me tonight. I’m… gonna head back first”

“Really? I can’t blame you after the night we just had. Well, goodnight Harry”

“Yeah... You too.” He replies briskly

Harry’s steps quicken when he’s out of sight of Ron. Harry hopes Ron doesn’t realize he left in the opposite direction of the dorms.

Harry runs through the maze of halls trying to catch up. The echoes of his steps in the halls would be deafening if it weren’t for the faint murmurs of frustration further ahead mingling with the noise. Finally reaching the courtyard, Harry sees Draecena facing away from him staring at the moon above, swallowing her tears. The moonlight on the dress shines, making her look like a statue in the throes of turmoil, trapped in marble. Harry decides to break the peace and walks in to meet her.

“I TOLD YOU NOT TO FOLLOW ME-” says Draecena as she whips around to face the intruder.

“Potter? What are you doing here?” Her face is flushed with anger, and her eyes glistening with frustration and the beginning of tears.

“I saw you run by and.. I don’t know. I wanted to-” Harry was cut off.

“Make fun of me? Didn’t I already make enough of a fool of myself tonight?”

Draecena is breathing heavily from her run across campus in her deep green gown. It's only this close that Harry realizes the dress’s golden neckline occasionally forms a snake head eating its tail before continuing along the dress. Running his eyes along the neckline is difficult as the dress shows much of her skin and cleavage. Her golden hair's disheveled state is corrected by Draecena while sweat glistens on its way down her temple. When his eyes finally trail back to meet hers, the look of frustration wracking her makes it hard for him to look away from their haunting silver hue.

“You certainly did,” Harry said with a grin.

“I don't want to hear that from YOU, half-blood. If only my date could muster a shred of decency or tact, I wouldn't be dealing with you on the night of the Yule Ball…” Draecena trails off while glaring heavily at Harry.

“Your date seemed to be going just fine till the end there. You looked good together for a pair of snakes. I only heard the sounds of muffled yelling and turned the corner just in time to catch you stomping on his foot and walking away. It was quite the show.” Harry says teasingly.

“My night was just ruined and you are here to tease me?! I just wanted a nice night to remember. The Yule Ball was supposed to be my moment to show off. I got the most beautiful dress, my makeup was perfect, and… I was excited that I might just have one nice romantic night,” Draecena's voice trails off while her voice begins to waver. “And instead I had to play babysitter to a fool and have none other than the perfect hero Potter chasing after me to rub it in my face.” Draecena scoffs, but the emotion in her voice is swallowed by the surfacing frustration.

“Was it really that bad?”

“You weren't there, Potter,” Draecena growls through gritted teeth. “I had to clean his shirt after dinner because he made a mess of his drink. I had to carry the shame of stumbling around during the dance because he lied about having a dance instructor. He was incompetent, something I’m sure you can relate to! Not to mention that look he gave me-”

“Oh, so he can dance better than I can! Are you just that much better than us?" says Harry, cutting her off.

“I think you would be the only one who couldn’t dance better than him, Potter,” quickly retorts Draecena.

“...Why don’t we  find out?”

Draecena's eyes go wide. She blushes a deep crimson at the offer. She wonders why such a strange challenge? To someone he is supposed to hate? Is this to make her feel even worse tonight?

Draecena stands there in the cold December air, collecting herself. She huffs out a few stifled hot breaths into the star-filled night. The long awkward pause is interrupted by her voice before she can consider the consequences of her next words.

“Sure, Potter, let's prove that you could never have been my date. But if you step on my toes like some blathering troll, I’m stopping our dance.”

Harry steps up to Draecena in a quick move, frustrated by her retort before realizing the proximity. Both are unable to be the one to invite the other in. In silent agreement, neither says anything as Harry’s right hand slides to Draecena's waist and Draecena's left hand is placed on his shoulder.

Grabbing Draecena’s other hand was a much higher hurdle. It was easy for Harry to get wrapped up in the atmosphere in the ballroom earlier and dance with Parvati, he didn’t even have time to think. Here, with only the stars as an audience and the harmony of their ragged breathing to dance to, it felt impossible. It’s Draecena’s gaze that breaks the tension. She looked up into his eyes like she was on the precipice of somewhere she knows she's not allowed to enter. Eyes full of indecision and desire she could not move past.

In one swift movement, Harry reaches down and grabs her free hand and holds it up to begin to dance. The feeling of his fingers sliding between hers feels as sensual as velvet. It hitches Harry’s breath. He would never say it, but as he looks down into Draecena’s eyes, he wants more. Harry shakes his head to remove the thought. His face is smothered in a deep heat. He looks back to Draecena to see her eyes hungrily consuming Harry’s every detail. Yet Harry’s intrusive thought lingers mouth curls into a grin.

“So you do have the guts to hold a woman tight. With how you danced with Parvati you had me fooled.”

“Shutup Malfoid”

“You know I hate that name…” she whispers.
“Just for right now, none of that.
call me Draecena.
not Malfoid,
not Draecena Malfoy,
not Malfoy,
just… Draecena”
Draecena’s head leans forward, and her forehead hits his chest before he can answer. Draecena, embarrassed by her bold request, tries desperately to hide her face.

“...you’ll fall behind Draecena.” Her head snaps back in surprise as Harry begins to pull her along in a slow dance. Almost tripping, Draecena falls into step, being led by the man she knows she wants to explore and cannot have.

Draecena can make the feelings drown and die out. Draecena can resist the urge to hold Harry, to stare at him. She is a Malfoy, a prodigy meant for greatness that no Halfblood could amount to. She is better than fickle crushes and emotions. But if Harry were the one to wrap her into his warm arms, if Harry were the one to yearn for her, if Harry were the one to give her that look, maybe… just maybe… that would prove that she’s allowed to have this?

Draecena begs to the void of her own thoughts, ‘please. Just let me have this.’

Wrapped up in each other's arms, with the tapping of their shoes on the courtyard cobbles their only quiet company, they dance.

Both steal awkward glances at the other, not sure if they are allowed to break the walls between them. Slowly, Harry feels Draecena’s body relax and fall into him. Her legs begin to brush against his while they move together. Her hand slides up his shoulder and around his neck, feeling the weight; Harry can't resist her pull.

Wanting more, Harry’s hand slides around to her low back, fingers mingling with the fabric of the dress like a lover's fingers digging into a duvet. Draecena looks up at Harry, not with surprise but a warm smile. A smile isolated from the world and the expectation of the pressures binding them. A moment where the push and pull games stop.

Harry’s heart hammers in his chest, reaching for Draecena.

After a long while of wordless dancing, the silence is interrupted by Harry’s whispered voice, worried that if he spoke too loud, it would break the fragile world they are in.

“I cut you off earlier before you finished complaining about your date tonight… Something about a look?”

“Why are you bringing him up again?"

“Just curious…” Harry struggles to suppress the jealousy seeping into the words.

“Ughhh… well. Yeah.” Draecena says slowly, as if deciding if she should admit the next part. “While dancing horribly in the ballroom, he kept pulling back to stare at my face… with this weird look. Like... like he wanted to kiss me.” Draecena forces out.

Surprised by the sudden confession, Harry’s foot unexpectedly gets stuck on the cobbles of the courtyard, causing him to fall hard to his right with Draecena. Catching himself, and more importantly Draecena, before they collapse to the ground. Draecena yelps in surprise and desperately latches onto Harry’s neck with both arms. If this wasn't an accident, it would have looked like Harry just pulled her into a deep dip. Faces barely apart, their hot breath in the freezing air begins to fog up Harry's glasses. They hold this moment for what feels like an eternity.

“He… he looked at me like you are Harry.” Draecena whispers

“...And why didn’t you kiss him?” Harry invites.

Because he wasn't you.

The words catch in her mouth.

Draecena’s thoughts are consumed by Harry. ‘Kiss me now, Harry, and I am yours. Kiss me now and break this pride I hold so dear. Close this gap and take my lips so I don't have to fight anymore. Take this pain of yearning away with just one kiss. Your kiss. You must be the one to break my curse. You have to be the one to save me. Please.’

Harry’s face twists as he realizes what he's doing and what he just said. And more importantly, who he just said it to. “I… guess I’m not suited to be your date with my fumbling feet.” Whispers Harry.

Draecena pulls away and stumbles backwards from Harry as fast as she can manage. She almost got pulled in by his ploy. His obvious trap.

“I knew it was only a matter of time for you Potter. Somehow managed to dance worse than him!” She shouts.

Draecena’s body realizes before she does that it's freezing outside in the winter air and shivers hard. “No more of the games, Potter, I’m cold, and it’s about time I retire for the night…” Her voice drifts off as she notices Harry taking off his jacket and draping it over her shoulders. The warmth hits her first in an overwhelming swell of emotions before being interrupted.  Draecena’s thoughts are enraptured by Harry’s white undershirt, partially soaked through and transparent with sweat, sticking to his collarbone. The top buttons are undone, and the tie is barely holding onto the knot that it started the night with. She looks down to avoid looking at him, only for her stomach to turn, seeing the Gryffindor emblem on the breast of the jacket over her shoulders, yet the warm smell invites her deeper.

Draecena feels her face aglow as she wants to curl into the jacket’s warmth and her resistance snaps.

“Give me these 4-eyes!” She reaches up and rips the glasses off Harry’s face and places them on the bridge of her own nose. “I’m shocked you can see anything with these!” Draecena struggles to stabilize herself with the distorted vision, but it’s the cost she needed to pay to make sure Harry can’t see. She leans into the coat to breathe in his warmth, refusing to show Harry this shameful side of her.

“Hey, what are you doing?!” Harry shouts as he reaches towards Draecena's general direction. Draecena would normal been able to dodge Harry without his glasses, it’s just unfortunate that her flushed face and embarrassment from the situation caused the glasses to fog up again. Harry wraps his arms around her carefully, not to hurt her but sure enough to catch her. He gently reaches down and pulls the glasses off her face, noticing that she’s not resisting.

Harry could hardly see through his glasses but managed a glimse of Draecena’s bright red and embarrassed face staring up at him. She briskly pushes forward and through Harry bumping him hard while he was attempting to clear his glasses.  They tumble out of his hand and onto the ground with a loud crack.

Harry sighs as he leans over to pick up his now-cracked glasses and almost misses Draecena whisper as she runs off to her dorm, taking his jacket with her,

“Goodnight Harry”

text:
(F) Pope Saint Damasus I

“Likewise it is decreed . . . that it ought to be announced that . . . the holy Roman Church has been placed at the forefront not by the conciliar decisions of other churches, but has received the primacy by the evangelic voice of our Lord and Savior, who says: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it; and I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven . . . ’ [Matt. 16:18–19]. The first see, therefore, is that of Peter the apostle, that of the Roman Church, which has neither stain nor blemish nor anything like it” (Decree of Damasus 3 [A.D. 382]).

(G) Saint Jerome

“‘But,’ you [Jovinian] will say, ‘it was on Peter that the Church was founded’ [Matt. 16:18]. Well . . . one among the twelve is chosen to be their head in order to remove any occasion for division” (Against Jovinian 1:26 [A.D. 393]).

(H) Pope Saint Innocent I

 “In seeking the things of God . . . you have acknowledged that judgment is to be referred to us [the pope], and have shown that you know that is owed to the Apostolic See [Rome], if all of us placed in this position are to desire to follow the apostle himself [Peter] from whom the episcopate itself and the total authority of this name have emerged” (Letters 29:1 [A.D. 408]).

(I) Saint Augustine

“Among these [apostles] Peter alone almost everywhere deserved to represent the whole Church. Because of that representation of the Church, which only he bore, he deserved to hear ‘I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven’” (Sermons 295:2 [A.D. 411]).

“Some things are said which seem to relate especially to the apostle Peter, and yet are not clear in their meaning unless referred to the Church, which he is acknowledged to have represented in a figure on account of the primacy which he bore among the disciples. Such is ‘I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven,’ and other similar passages” (Commentary on Psalm 108 1 [A.D. 415]).

“Who is ignorant that the first of the apostles is the most blessed Peter?” (Commentary on John 56:1 [A.D. 416]).

(J) Council of Ephesus 

“Philip, presbyter and legate of [Pope Celestine I] said: ‘We offer our thanks to the holy and venerable synod, that when the writings of our holy and blessed pope had been read to you . . . you joined yourselves to the holy head also by your holy acclamations. For your blessedness is not ignorant that the head of the whole faith, the head of the apostles, is blessed Peter the apostle’” (Acts of the Council, session 2 [A.D. 431]).
“Philip, the presbyter and legate of the Apostolic See [Rome] said: ‘There is no doubt, and in fact it has been known in all ages, that the holy and most blessed Peter, prince and head of the apostles, pillar of the faith, and foundation of the Catholic Church, received the keys of the kingdom from our Lord Jesus Christ, the Savior and Redeemer of the human race, and that to him was given the power of loosing and binding sins: who down even to today and forever both lives and judges in his successors’” (ibid., session 3).

(K) Pope Saint Leo I

“Our Lord Jesus Christ . . . has placed the principal charge on the blessed Peter, chief of all the apostles, and from him as from the head wishes his gifts to flow to all the body, so that anyone who dares to secede from Peter’s solid rock may understand that he has no part or lot in the divine mystery. He wished him who had been received into partnership in his undivided unity to be named what he himself was, when he said: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church’ [Matt. 16:18], that the building of the eternal temple might rest on Peter’s solid rock, strengthening his Church so surely that neither could human rashness assail it nor the gates of hell prevail against it” (Letters 10:1 [A.D. 445).

text:
The Creator doesn't force any of his creation to love Him. It's a choice. lucifer had it all... his beauty, wisdom, elevated status and free will turned into self-exaltation. “I will ascend… I will make myself like the Most High.” A creature of high rank sought the place that only belongs only to the Creator. Violence and corruption followed that pride.

The second part of your question is another subject entirely. This is the long answer...

Your objection assumes two things that the 'Christian' claim does not actually require: that the destination is a blank, and that people are straining to earn a place in it.

On the first point, the texts do not leave the promise entirely undescribed. Revelation 21–22 pictures a new heaven and a new earth in which the former order has passed away. God dwells with people. Death, mourning, crying, and pain are gone. There is no temple, because the presence itself is the light. The river and the tree of life are there; nothing unclean enters.

It is restoration and fulfillment, not an empty abstraction. Earlier lines point the same direction: creation set free from corruption, a city whose builder is God, an inheritance that does not fade. The details are partial... vision rather than a floor plan... but they are not “no one knows anything.”

On the second point, the offer is framed as a gift, not a prize for effort. “The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” “By grace you have been saved through faith… it is the gift of God, not a result of works.”

The condition named is trust in what has already been done, not a successful climb toward an unknown reward. People are not described as 'trying to get there' so much as receiving a promise as a gift that has been held out.

So the sentence “no one knows what it will be like, but everyone is trying to get there” misstates both halves. The promise is sketched, and the way in is given, not achieved. 

The logic of the claim itself is not “chase a blank.” It is “a described restoration is offered as a gift.”

text:
One of the scariest realizations I've come to in scripture is that much - if not most - of the idolatry Israel committed in the Old Testament wasn't generic worship of random false gods, but a careful and deliberate blending of idolatry with the genuine worship of Jehovah.

When Aaron made the golden calf in Sinai, he didn't say "I made a new god, his name is Bob!" Rather, those involved said "these be *thy* gods, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt."

Later, when Jeroboam instituted idolatry after the kingdom split, he didn't say "I have invented newer, better gods!" Rather, he said "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt."

Interestingly, the following verses say that this *became* sin to the children of Israel.

In both instances, it was not pitched as departure from Jehovah, but a "fresh take" on the stale religion they knew.

A deconstruction, if you will.

Then in II Kings 16, we read this:

"And king Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglathpileser king of Assyria, and saw an altar that was at Damascus: and king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the workmanship thereof.
And Urijah the priest built an altar according to all that king Ahaz had sent from Damascus: so Urijah the priest made it against king Ahaz came from Damascus.
And when the king was come from Damascus, the king saw the altar: and the king approached to the altar, and offered thereon.
And he burnt his burnt offering and his meat offering, and poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings, upon the altar.
And he brought also the brasen altar, which was before the Lord, from the forefront of the house, from between the altar and the house of the Lord, and put it on the north side of the altar.
And king Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, Upon the great altar burn the morning burnt offering, and the evening meat offering, and the king's burnt sacrifice, and his meat offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their meat offering, and their drink offerings; and sprinkle upon it all the blood of the burnt offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice: and the brasen altar shall be for me to enquire by.
Thus did Urijah the priest, according to all that king Ahaz commanded."

Once again, while we see earlier that Ahaz was evil and did indeed sacrifice to other gods, that's not what is described here.  Rather, he was attempting to modernize and put his own spin on the traditional worship in the temple - maintaining the sacrifices, but updating the methods and styles to suit his own tastes, which were based on envy of the glamorous pagan world.

In the next chapter, as the northern kingdom of Israel goes into captivity, we read this: "And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the Lord their God, and they built them high places in all their cities..."

Secretly. Not openly.

Even under wicked, pagan kings, the idolatry was kept secret, or given a pretense of true worship. This is why, in the prophets, we frequently read of Israel complaining of God's unfairness in judgement, claiming to have followed him faithfully.

They had convinced themselves that their idolatry was actually glorifying to God.

And then in the final act of the chapter, we read this:

"And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof.
And so it was at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they feared not the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them, which slew some of them.
Wherefore they spake to the king of Assyria, saying, The nations which thou hast removed, and placed in the cities of Samaria, know not the manner of the God of the land: therefore he hath sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they know not the manner of the God of the land.
Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, Carry thither one of the priests whom ye brought from thence; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the manner of the God of the land.
Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Bethel, and taught them how they should fear the Lord.
Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities wherein they dwelt."

This was the northern kingdom of Israel, not Judah. 

They had abandoned God many generations ago, and been ruled by unrepentant, pagan kings. They had killed the prophets. They were being judged, and were removed from the land and replaced by foreigners.

So when the lion-killings began, they realized they had offended God (which they deemed to be geographic in nature - see Michael Heiser's work for more on this), and called for a priest.

But that priest wasn't of the order of Aaron, or of the Levites. That priest was not sanctioned by God in the law of Moses. Under Jeroboam, we are told specifically that he made priests out of the lowest of the people, specifically to make a break with the Levitical order that remained loyal to the house of David.

So this was a priest of Jeroboam's order of the golden calves, dwelling in Bethel, where one of the calves was located, yet he "taught them how they should fear the Lord" even as they continued their own idolatry in private.

This scares me, and it should scare you, because it's happening all around us right now, throughout the Western Church.

Our tendency as people has always been to mix the holy with the profane, and enjoy the middle ground that looks nice, but demands little.

Looking back it's easy to see that influence through all of church history (starting with the imported pagan trappings of AD 300 and going all the way through Osteen's prosperity gospel and the seeker-friendly movement of the past few decades).

But it's happening now, in our homes and churches too.
How many of us flip through our Bibles and hymnals at church, then come home and worship a screen? Or a house? Or a career? Or lust? Or convenience?

And of those, how many are convinced within themselves that they are still in a right relationship with God, and are confused by conviction and judgement, when it finds them?

This thought, for me, brings into sharp relief many warnings of the New Testament as well. Test yourself, prove yourself, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

If deception were obvious, it wouldn't be deception.

See it, face it, reject it - even when it hides behind a devout and pious facade.

God help us to seek out the old paths once again and walk faithfully in them, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left.

text:
The slogan featured prominently across the image—"GOD STANDS WITH ISRAEL REGARDLESS"—is one of the most anti-scriptural assertions a teacher of the Bible can make.   Throughout the Law and the Prophets, the phrase "regardless" is utterly foreign to God's covenant with Israel. God never offered blanket, unconditional moral immunity to any nation, people, or king. The covenant was explicitly bound to justice, righteousness, and obedience:
The Conditional Warning of the Law: "And if you defile the land, it will vomit you out as it vomited out the nations that were before you." (Leviticus 18:28)
The Rebuking of Presumption: When ancient Israel claimed God's presence guaranteed their military and physical security "regardless" of their behavior, the prophet Jeremiah confronted them directly at the Temple gate: "Do not trust in deceptive words and say, 'This is the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord!' If you really change your ways and your actions and deal with each other justly, if you do not oppress the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow and do not shed innocent blood in this place... then I will let you live in this place." (Jeremiah 7:4–7)
Amos Shatters National Superiority: When the people presumed God was unconditionally on their side against their enemies, God declared through Amos: "Are not you Israelites the same to me as the Cushites? Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor and the Arameans from Kir?" (Amos 9:7)
The graphic attempts to stitch together disparate verses to manufacture a modern geopolitical blank check:
Hosea 2:16 ("He is Her Husband"): Hosea’s entire prophetic ministry was a living indictment of Israel's spiritual adultery and idolatry. God called the nation Lo-Ammi—"Not My People" (Hosea 1:9). Redemptive restoration in Hosea is rooted in genuine repentance and turning back to God in fidelity, not an endorsement of secular state violence while rejecting God's laws.
Jeremiah 31:35–37 ("An Unconditional Covenant"): The text immediately preceding those verses (Jeremiah 31:31–34) defines the exact covenant being discussed: The New Covenant. Hebrews 8:8–13 quotes this passage explicitly, declaring that the Old Covenant is obsolete and that the New Covenant is sealed in the blood of Jesus Christ, written on the hearts of believers—not on an ethnic registry or a political map.
Revelation 20:1–6 ("He Will Reign in Israel"): The text of Revelation 20 makes zero mention of the modern nation-state of Israel or a geopolitical regime. It speaks of the souls of martyrs and those who did not worship the beast reigning with Christ.
When ministers proclaim that God stands with any secular state "regardless," they commit the exact sin Jeremiah warned against: crying "Peace, peace, when there is no peace" (Jeremiah 6:14) and baptizing human realpolitik in holy water. True fidelity to God demands naming injustice wherever it occurs, not granting divine waivers for slaughter.
