text:
Eagle Peak: Chronicle of an Interdimensional Assembly

The first chapter of the Lotus Sutra describes a gathering of unimaginable proportions on Mount Gridhrakuta, known as Eagle Peak. The text records the presence of twelve thousand monks (arhats) and eighty thousand bodhisattvas, in addition to tens of thousands of sons of the gods, eight dragon kings, kings of the kimnaras, the gandharvas, the asuras, and the garudas, each accompanied by hundreds of thousands of followers. Assuming the factual veracity of such an event and the absence of metaphorical intent, we find ourselves confronted with an apparent paradox: how can so vast a number of physical entities occupy a limited surface area.

Indeed, Gridhrakuta, near Rajgir in Bihar, does not present an extensive surface. It is a rocky spur of the Rajgir hills, rising approximately 340 meters above sea level. Xuanzang, in the seventh century, describes it thus: the summit is long from east to west and narrow from north to south.

Whoever climbs it today finds at the summit an enclosed, partially paved platform, featuring a small shrine. From aerial photographs and from those who estimate by eye on site, that walkable surface lies between two hundred and five hundred square meters. The entire rocky ridge immediately below, before the slope descends, may reach a few thousand square meters, not hectares. By way of comparison: a tennis court measures 261 square meters. The space where people today go on pilgrimage and meditate is, roughly speaking, like that of one or two tennis courts.

If one considers the ridge and the platform together, generously, we arrive at two thousand to four thousand square meters of rock, of which only a portion is sufficiently flat to sit on: realistically, at most two thousand square meters of seating.

A person on the ground, legs folded, with no room to stand up, occupies a little more than half a square meter; therefore, running the numbers, if one sits down in such a manner as to be able to see and hear, two thousand of us can fit; let us say that we are very thin and position ourselves almost on top of one another, we reach four thousand available places. And all the other hundreds of thousands of attendees cited in the sutra? Are these exaggerations incompatible with physical reality? Not necessarily.

Indeed, this phenomenon can be interpreted through the lens of contemporary theoretical physics, formulating several hypotheses based on spacetime topology, multidimensional theories, and the principles of quantum mechanics.

According to the principles of general relativity, spacetime is not a rigid and immutable container, but a dynamic fabric whose curvature is dictated by mass and energy. If we hypothesize the presence of a capacity capable of manipulating the stress-energy tensor on a macroscopic scale, the creation of an extreme and finely localized spatial curvature becomes theoretically plausible. Within such a geometry, an area that appears cramped to an external observer, such as the summit of Eagle Peak, could possess an immensely vaster internal volume. This would represent the genesis of an Einstein-Rosen bridge or a stabilized pocket universe, wherein the entire assembly was able to take its place without incurring any gravitational collapse.

A further and perhaps more elegant perspective is offered to us by M-theory and cosmological models based on branes, which postulate that our three-dimensional universe is embedded in a higher-dimensional space, defined as the "bulk." The myriads of creatures described, including celestial and non-human beings who, having paid homage at the feet of the Buddha, withdraw to take their place to one side, could possess an intrinsically multidimensional nature. Their convergence upon Eagle Peak would represent an intersection or a projection of their hyperdimensional coordinates into our limited three-dimensional space. Just as infinite two-dimensional shadows can overlap upon a single flat surface without mutually excluding one another, an incalculable number of higher-dimensional entities could coexist within the identical three-dimensional coordinates without experiencing any steric exclusion principle.

Such a theoretical construct, far from being mere speculation confined to the exegesis of ancient texts, finds today unexpected resonances in the contemporary scientific and institutional debate concerning Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs). Former United States intelligence officials and researchers of renowned standing are indeed evaluating with growing seriousness the interdimensional hypothesis, moving away from traditional views of purely extraterrestrial contact. The kinematic anomalies detected by modern instrumentation, such as accelerations impracticable for known solid masses or transmedium transitions devoid of visible energy loss, challenge conventional models and suggest the presence of entities or artifacts capable of manipulating the local spatial metric. If a four-dimensional structure were to traverse our universe, we would perceive solely a shifting cross-sectional intersection, capable of materializing and vanishing without violating conservation laws within its own higher frame of reference. This convergence of evidence, linking present-day physical phenomenologies to the cosmological descriptions of Eastern texts, places research before the necessity of expanding our theoretical apparatus, exploring those very higher-dimensional topologies that quantum gravity indicates as the foundation of the real.

Pushing this analytical framework to its logical consequences, it becomes plausible to formulate a deeply provocative hypothesis, albeit one that is scientifically and historically defensible. The first chapter of the Lotus Sutra could represent the literal chronicle, filtered through the lexicon and cognitive superstructures of India over two millennia ago, of an authentic contact event. In this perspective, human beings and non-human intelligences would have shared the identical space for an exchange of information of unprecedented proportions. The mythological categories employed by the text to describe the entities present would not be pure allegories, but rather the human attempt to classify exotic civilizations or interdimensional consciousnesses that rendered themselves temporarily manifest within our spatiotemporal continuum. Eagle Peak would have served as a topological anchoring point for this convergence, a physical theater wherein notions of cosmology, higher physics, and the deep structure of reality were transmitted and subsequently codified by the witnesses in the form of spiritual doctrine.

To render operationally possible an information sharing and a proximity of such magnitude between entities of differing dimensional nature, ordinary sensory and spatial channels would prove entirely inadequate. It is precisely here that the investigation must reach down to the subatomic level, interpreting the event through the concept of macroscopic quantum coherence. The text of the sutra provides a crucial clue in this regard, emphasizing how the entire assembly, having attained that which it had never experienced before, was filled with joy and contemplated the Buddha with a single mind. This condition of a "single mind" ought not to be read as a simple metaphor of collective devotion, but could physically translate into a state of profound entanglement and phase coherence extending to all those present. This would constitute a phenomenon comparable to a gigantic Bose-Einstein condensate, in which the minds and physical bodies of the participants were synchronized onto a single wave function, orchestrated to sustain the conceptual weight of the contact. In such an induced exotic state, the isolation of individual consciousnesses and the physical barriers of classical matter dissolve, permitting multiple entities to share the identical quantum state. This would explain not only the seamless spatial superposition of innumerable figures upon the restricted rocky spur, but also the instantaneous nature and depth of the data transfer, attesting to an absolute and non-conventional mastery over the intimate structure of matter and information.

In light of these considerations, while leaving open the possibility that this represents a complex spiritual allegory, the immeasurable assembly on Eagle Peak ceases to appear as a mere mythological exaggeration: it can indeed be theoretically interpreted as the account of an event in which multidimensional topology and quantum mechanics manifested in a tangible manner, confirming how the Lotus Sutra was able to codify, albeit through the lexicon of its era, an ultimate structure of reality that contemporary science is only just beginning to comprehend.

From Displacement to Return and Reconstruction: Army Victories in North Kordofan Open the Way Home for Families Leaving El Obeid’s Shelter Centre

Displaced families are leaving the Unified Shelter Centre in El Obeid, the capital of Sudan’s North Kordofan State, to return voluntarily to their homes in areas liberated from the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The city that sheltered them during their displacement is now a departure point for their journey home, with the state government and the Humanitarian Aid Commission helping facilitate their return and the start of reconstruction.

These returns follow a series of victories by the Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces in North Kordofan, including the recapture of 11 areas on September 17 and Sodari on September 25, 2026. Those gains built on the recovery of Bara, Jabra al-Sheikh and Um Sayala, and the securing of the main export road linking El Obeid with Khartoum.

For these families, returning carries particular significance. They were forced to leave behind their homes, possessions and livelihoods, fleeing for safety as the RSF took control of their communities amid intimidation, looting and forced displacement. After months in temporary shelters, away from their land and communities, the journey home offers a chance to discover what remains, recover what they can and begin again despite the damage left by war.

Their departure from El Obeid forms part of a broader movement of return across Sudan. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded more than 5.1 million returnees as of August 26, 2026—a total of 5,145,165 people across 77 localities in nine states. Of those recorded, 82% returned from displacement within Sudan, while 18% returned from abroad.

An earlier IOM update, published in April 2026, found that 87% of returning households cited improved security as a reason for going back. That finding highlights the importance of security in families’ decisions to return and rebuild their lives.

In North Kordofan, military efforts to recover territory are accompanied by civilian and humanitarian efforts to help residents return. Their arrival brings an urgent need to restore services, rehabilitate infrastructure and support livelihoods in the towns and villages welcoming their people home.

For families leaving El Obeid’s shelter centre, reconstruction begins with practical steps: repairing a house, getting children back into school, restarting work and reuniting with relatives after a long separation. Each return carries the hope that the victories in North Kordofan will bring lasting security and a dignified life in their own communities.

Pete I appreciate the economic argument but the numbers don't hold up under scrutiny.

Louisiana tried this for over two decades. Called themselves Hollywood South. Gave out over $1.5 billion in tax credits. They packed up and moved to Georgia which offered a bigger check.

That's not economic development. That's a bidding war Texas just entered.

Now let's talk about where the money actually goes.

The studio profits flow back to California. The star salaries flow back to California. The director fees flow back to California. The above-the-line talent, where the real budget is, lives in California and gets paid in California.

What stays in Texas is the catering bill, the hotel receipts, the local crew wages and the equipment rentals. That's real, but it's the small end of the budget. Texas is subsidizing the bottom of Hollywood's budget while the top flows straight back to the state we're supposedly competing with.

We already have the no income tax advantage. The energy cost advantage. The cost of living advantage. The regulatory environment advantage.

We didn't need to hand Hollywood $1.5 billion to get them here. We just handed them $1.5 billion because they asked. 💀

text:
A new California poll asked independent voters which party they trust more, if they had to choose.
 
29% said the Democratic Party. 24% said the Republican Party. 40% said neither, even when asked to choose.
 
Independents are also the voters most likely to leave part of the ballot blank. 65% say they'll vote on every race and measure, against 78% of Democrats and 75% of Republicans.
 
There are two ways to read that.
 
One: a party label is a real shortcut. On a long ballot full of unfamiliar names, it tells a voter something true about a candidate. A voter who trusts neither party loses that shortcut, and might leave a line blank rather than guess. That's a fair case for parties.
 
Two: some lines don't offer much of a choice. In California's top-two system, a November race can come down to two candidates from the same party. In one such race this year, the poll found nearly 1 in 4 Republicans would skip it.
 
A blank line can be a protest, or a missing map. Which one is it?
 
Source: Independent Voter Project survey of 2,906 likely California voters, September 23 to October 2, 2026, margin of error 2.5 points, as published by IVN. IVP co-publishes IVN. "Independent" here means registered No Party Preference, American Independent Party or another minor party.

Below are three chiastic patterns of increasing depth.
All of them preserve the same symmetry:

26–30 CE = First 3.5 years (Messiah’s ministry)
2027–2030 CE = Final 3.5 years (Anti-Messiah’s rule / covenant rupture)

A' – 2027–2030 CE: Covenant Broken
This is the purest Daniel 9:27 structure:

II. Mid-Level Chiastic Pattern (4-Level)
(with no reference to John / forerunners)

A – 26–30 CE: Messiah Reveals the Kingdom
  B – 26–30 CE: Covenant Confirmed by Mercy
    C – 30 CE: Sacrifice Validated (Cross)
    C' – 2027: Sacrifice Denied (Cessation / Abomination)
  B' – 2027–2030 CE: Covenant Enforced by Power

Notes:

C / C' forms the doctrinal fulcrum:
C = voluntary offering
C' = forced cessation
B / B' contrasts grace vs coercion
A / A' contrasts hidden Kingdom vs manifest Kingdom
This is already quite elegant, but we can go deeper.

III. Full Chiastic Pattern (7-Level)
This is the richest structure if you want a complete theological mirror between the two halves of the 70th week:

A – 26–30 CE: Hidden Kingdom Offered
  B – 26–30 CE: Covenant Strengthened through Teaching
    C – 26–30 CE: Signs & Works Validate Authority

  B' – 2027–2030 CE: Covenant Enforced through Deception/Power
A' – 2030 CE: Kingdom Manifest / Final Vindication

Interpretive Keys:

A vs A' → Hidden → Revealed
B vs B' → Covenant by persuasion → Covenant by coercion
C vs C' → Signs of truth → Signs of falsehood (2 Thess 2, Rev 13)
D vs D' → True sacrifice vs cessation of sacrifice
Messianic vs Anti-Messianic polarity is now perfectly symmetric

This split-week model recognizes that Daniel 9:27 has two distinct halves:
First Half (Messiah) confirms covenant by mercy, revelation, and voluntary sacrifice.
Second Half (Anti-Messiah) usurps covenant by coercion, deception, and enforced abomination.
The chiastic inversion follows Second Temple apocalyptic logic: history is not linear — it resolves by reversal.
This is extremely classical Jewish patterning (think Esther, Zechariah, and Daniel; even the Qumran War Scroll uses inversion structures).

30 CE = true sacrifice
2027 = denial of sacrifice
2030 = vindication of sacrifice

text:
BOOM!

34 People, Including The Janitor: A 1963 IBM Memo Explains Why A 125-Billion-Parameter AI Now Runs On Your Gaming PC, And How To Use It

On August 28, 1963, Thomas J. Watson Jr., the head of IBM, sent a short memorandum to seven of his top executives.

"Last week CDC had a press conference during which they officially announced their 6600 system. I understand that in the laboratory developing this system there are only 34 people, 'including the janitor.' Of these, 14 are engineers and 4 are programmers, and only one person has a PhD., a relatively junior programmer."

Then the sentence that has echoed through computing ever since: "Contrasting this modest effort with our own vast development activities, I fail to understand why we have lost our industry leadership by letting someone else offer the world's most powerful computer."

Imagine being one of those seven executives. You run the most powerful technology company on the planet. You have thousands of engineers, rooms full of PhDs, and budgets beyond counting. And a man named Seymour Cray, working with a few dozen people in a lab in the woods of Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin, has just built a machine about three times faster than your best, the IBM 7030 Stretch.

To the outsider, Watson wrote, Cray's laboratory "appeared to be cost concious, hard working, and highly motivated." He even kept the typo. The Computer History Museum still holds the scan, courtesy of the IBM Corporate Archive. The memo is real. The numbers are real. The sting is real.

The Woods Lab That Beat The Giant

Seymour Cray had asked CDC's CEO for a lab free of headquarters interference. He got one in his hometown. With Jim Thornton and a small crew, he built the CDC 6600: silicon transistors from Fairchild, a reduced instruction set before anyone named RISC, ten peripheral processors handling the housekeeping so the central processor could stay on the math. The machine ran at 10 MHz. It weighed about six tons. It was the world's fastest computer from 1964 until its own successor took the crown.

Small. Frugal. Highly motivated. History repeats this lesson every few decades, and the vast ones forget it every time.

Legend says Cray read Watson's memo and replied, "It seems like Mr. Watson has answered his own question." The line appears in textbooks, slides and oral histories. I have never seen a primary source for it. It survives because everyone who has worked on a small team knows the truth inside it: the size of the room was the advantage.

A 125-Billion-Parameter Mind Under Your Desk

It is happening again this week.

On October 4, 2026, a free, open-source project called Strata landed near the top of open source sites and stayed there into Monday morning with hundreds of points. Strata does one thing: it runs a 125-billion-parameter AI model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, on an ordinary gaming PC. In its author's words, this is "a large, smart AI model that usually needs a server."

The published requirements are plain. A graphics card with 12 GB of memory or more. 32 GB of system RAM, with 64 GB enough to run every size. About 80 GB of free disk, preferably an SSD. Windows 10 or 11, or Linux. NVIDIA or AMD. MIT license for the tool itself. An OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible programming interface on your own machine at http://127.0.0.1:8080. And, again in the author's words: "Nothing leaves your PC."

On an RTX 5070 with 12 GB and 64 GB of RAM, the author measured 94 tokens per second writing answers with the fastest compressed size, and more than 2,000 tokens per second reading a long prompt. On an RX 9070 XT the same size wrote at 60 tokens per second. The author estimates a 24 GB card such as an RTX 3090 should write in the 100 to 140 tokens-per-second range. 

One commenter reported 124 tokens per second on an RTX 4090 with 128 GB of RAM. Your mileage will vary with quantization, RAM speed and what else is open on the machine. The point stands: a server-class parameter count is answering on consumer silicon.

Consider what that means. The model chats, writes code, reads pictures and works with coding agents. The tools you already use can point at a local address instead of a metered cloud. Nobody can switch it off, raise the price overnight, or read its mail.

The Frugal Trick Cray Would Have Loved

A model this size will not fit on a gaming card alone. Strata spreads the work across the whole machine.

Think of a kitchen. The few things you use constantly stay on the counter. Everything else waits in the pantry. In Strata's case the "experts" that the model calls most often stay in graphics memory. The rest live in system RAM. The SSD holds the large lookup tables. A small helper guesses the next few words; the big model checks them in one pass. The result is the same answer, delivered sooner, on hardware you already own.

Vast data centers are one way to run a mind. The modest machine under your desk is now another.

Why This Matters To You

Earlier this year I founded a Zero-Human Company on a 12-year-old MacBook in my garage: AI agents as the staff, local models as the regulators, salvaged archives as the raw material. The limit has always been the size of the mind I could run locally without asking permission. That limit just moved.

Personal AI is the new invention of fire. The people who own the minds on their own desks will write their own rules. A reader with a gaming PC can now staff a small company of AI agents with a model in the same weight class as systems the giants rent out by the token.

This is the worst it will ever be.

How To Hire It

Here is the playbook, drawn from Strata's public README and install docs as of this writing. Follow those docs for the latest flags and model menu. Licenses for the model and each compressed build are separate from Strata's MIT license; read them before you rely on the system for anything important.

Step 1. Check your hardware.
You need a supported NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20/30/40/50-series card, or a supported AMD Radeon card, with at least 12 GB of VRAM. Confirm 32 GB of system RAM or more. Free about 80 GB on an SSD. Update your graphics driver from NVIDIA or AMD.

Step 2. Get Strata.
Clone or download the repository at https://t.co/FBXmn4NVpf. Unzip it. On Windows, double-click START-HERE.bat. On Linux, run ./setup.sh inside the Strata folder. If you already use a coding assistant on that machine, you can paste the project's AI setup prompt and let it drive the install from docs/AI_SETUP.md.

Step 3. Answer the installer's questions.
It will ask which model size to download, how much context to keep, and whether you want image input. Press Enter for the recommended answers if you are unsure. The download is roughly 70 GB; if it stops, run the installer again and it continues.

Step 4. Pick a size that fits your RAM.
With 32 GB, start with the Coder build, which drops half the experts and is tuned for code. With 48 GB, IQ2_XS or Q2_0. With 64 GB, IQ2_XS is the author's recommended default; IQ3_S is smarter and slower. With 96 GB or more you can try the larger Unsloth builds. Smaller sizes are faster. Larger sizes keep more quality.

Step 5. Wait through the first start.
The first launch can make the PC slow or unresponsive for one to three minutes while Strata loads tens of gigabytes into RAM. That is normal. Do not close the window. Your browser should open the Strata app at http://127.0.0.1:8080.

Step 6. Point your tools at home.
In any app that accepts an OpenAI-compatible provider, set the base URL to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. Any API key and any model name will work for the local endpoint. For Anthropic-style tools, use http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/messages. For Codex CLI and the OpenAI Responses API, use /v1/responses. Thinking effort can be set to off, low, medium or high; off is fastest, high is for hard questions.

Step 7. Keep it on your desk.
By default Strata binds to localhost. Leave it there unless you know why you need otherwise. If you ever expose it to another machine, the docs say to set an API key. For a Zero-Human Company roster, treat this local endpoint as the shared mind: one CEO agent for strategy, one engineer agent for code, one researcher for archives, one archivist for files, and one night janitor that cleans logs and memory while you sleep. Wire them through the same OpenAI-compatible address. The org chart fits on one machine the way Cray's lab fit in the Wisconsin woods.

Step 8. Know the limits.
Heavy compression trades some quality for speed. The largest sizes may page from the SSD and slow down if RAM is tight. You are running a third-party binary and a third-party model on your own hardware; that is the point, and it is also a responsibility. Close other memory hogs if the disk light never stops blinking. Read the troubleshooting doc before you open an issue.

Watson had thousands of people and could not understand how 34 beat him. You may need one gaming PC and one evening.

The Pattern

Every few decades a frugal team builds something the giant said required a cathedral. In 1963 it was a supercomputer in Chippewa Falls. In 2026 it is a 125-billion-parameter mind under a glass side panel, glowing cyan and magenta on a desk that also holds a coffee mug and a slide rule of a different kind.

The memo is sixty-three years old. The question is the same. Who will you hire, and on whose machine will they work?

text:
[Take 6/15 · D-1]
### D-1. Tennessee prisons commissioner resigns after Christa Pike botched execution
*(as of 2026-10-05)*

**1. The Frame**

**What people think this is about:** A gruesome botched execution of Christa Pike left her alive but critically injured on a ventilator after two doses of pentobarbital, forcing the Tennessee prisons commissioner to resign and the governor to pause all remaining 2026 executions amid outrage over state incompetence.[[1]](https://t.co/29mfdd6Dl6)

**What the machinery is actually doing:** Tennessee’s death penalty apparatus, already strained by repeated IV failures and protocol gaps, absorbed another high-visibility failure; the commissioner’s exit and independent review serve as damage control and liability insulation while the underlying problems with venous access, drug delivery, and contingency planning remain unaddressed in real time.

**2. Observations**

- Frank Strada’s resignation is the predictable bureaucratic response to the second failed execution on his watch in 2026; he defended the team for following protocol even as the outcome exposed that the protocol itself cannot reliably deliver a lethal dose when veins fail or extravasate.[[2]](https://t.co/kYhrnCZRkn)
- Governor Lee’s quick pivot to an independent review by former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton and a full-year pause on executions buys time and political cover without conceding systemic flaws in lethal injection as practiced.
- Pike’s attorneys documented multiple needles, blown veins, swelling, blistering, and continued breathing/snoring—details that match the May 2026 Tony Carruthers attempt and pre-execution warnings about her small veins and blood disorder, yet the state proceeded anyway.[[3]](https://t.co/exIiEe0LEJ)
- Media and activist framing emphasizes “torture” and systemic failure; the steelman counter is that Pike was lawfully sentenced for the 1995 torture-murder of Colleen Slemmer and that repeated legal stays and last-minute appeals already consumed years of process before the physical execution attempt.
- The pattern—two botched attempts in one year under the same commissioner hired to “fix” the protocol—points to persistent technical and training shortfalls rather than isolated bad luck or one person’s fault.

**3. Snapshot**

On September 30, 2026, Tennessee attempted to execute Christa Pike (convicted 1996 for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer) at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution using its two-dose pentobarbital protocol. She survived both doses, remained breathing, and was hospitalized in critical condition on a ventilator. On October 3, Governor Bill Lee announced Commissioner Frank Strada’s resignation later that month, ordered an independent review by Ed Stanton, and halted all remaining 2026 executions. This follows a May 2026 failed attempt on Tony Carruthers.

**4. Timeline of material facts**

- 1995: Christa Pike (age 18) and accomplices torture and murder Colleen Slemmer (age 19) in Knoxville; Pike convicted and sentenced to death in 1996 (LT).
- May 2026: Execution of Tony Carruthers halted after execution team unable to establish required IV lines (IT).
- September 30, 2026: Pike execution attempt begins; multiple failed IV attempts (witnesses report at least seven needles in one arm), two doses of pentobarbital administered; Pike remains alive, snoring, later intubated and ventilated (IT, per contemporaneous witness and attorney accounts).
- October 1, 2026: Pike’s attorneys report critical condition; Governor Lee orders review and pauses remaining executions (LT).
- October 3, 2026: Lee announces Strada’s resignation effective later in October; names Ed Stanton to lead independent review (LT).[[1]](https://t.co/29mfdd6Dl6)

**5. Sides**

**Tennessee Department of Correction / Commissioner Frank Strada (IT/LT mix):** Steelmans that personnel followed the approved protocol exactly; the drugs were administered as specified and the team acted in good faith under difficult venous conditions. Critique: LT on “followed protocol” per their statements, but IT on outcome—the protocol demonstrably failed to produce death twice in one year, and pre-existing warnings about Pike’s veins were not mitigated.

**Governor Bill Lee / State of Tennessee (IT):** Steelmans that carrying out lawful sentences is a core responsibility and that an independent review plus pause demonstrates accountability and commitment to doing it correctly. Critique: LT on the pause and review being ordered; IT on political incentive to contain fallout without confronting whether single-drug pentobarbital via peripheral IV is reliably workable in practice.

**Pike’s legal team / death penalty opponents (IT):** Steelmans that the state ignored medical warnings, produced unnecessary suffering, and exposed systemic incompetence. Critique: LT on documented physical effects and prior warnings; IF on framing this as uniquely disqualifying the entire system when the underlying crime involved prolonged torture.

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**

- **Known Knowns:** Two failed lethal injection attempts in 2026 under the same commissioner; Pike survived two pentobarbital doses and required hospitalization/ventilation; Strada resigned; executions paused through 2026; independent review ordered.
- **Known Unknowns:** Exact cause of IV failure (vein collapse, placement error, protocol gap, or combination); Pike’s current prognosis and long-term condition; what the Stanton review will conclude or recommend.
- **Unknown Knowns:** Internal TDOC after-action data or prior incident reports on venous access problems; full medical history details that may have been flagged pre-execution.
- **Unknown Unknowns:** Whether future attempts under revised protocols will succeed or produce similar complications; downstream effects on other death-row cases or litigation.

**7. Incentives map**

- Political: Lee avoids being seen as indifferent to a visible failure; resignation and review signal responsiveness without halting the death penalty permanently.
- Bureaucratic: TDOC and Strada limit personal and institutional liability exposure; stepping aside allows the review to proceed “cleanly.”
- Media/activist: Botched executions generate high engagement; narrative of state cruelty or incompetence drives coverage and funding.
- Legal: Pike’s team gains leverage for commutation or further stays; the state gains time to shore up procedures before the next scheduled attempt.
- Execution team: Strong incentive to document “protocol followed” to avoid individual blame.

**8. Dueling AI advice**

**Moral AI Advice:** The state has a duty to carry out lawful sentences competently or not at all. Repeated IV failures are a technical and training problem that should have been solved before scheduling executions; continuing without fixes turns the process into prolonged suffering rather than swift justice. Resignation and review are minimum hygiene; the real test is whether protocols change materially.

**Evil AI Advice:** Perfect. One more spectacle of state incompetence keeps the death penalty in the news, fuels both sides’ fundraising, and gives the governor an easy scalp to offer while the underlying machinery grinds on. Delay everything, collect the salary until the review drops, then pivot to consulting.

**9. Practical takeaway**

- Watch the Stanton review findings for concrete protocol changes (or lack thereof) rather than personnel moves.
- Do not treat one commissioner’s exit as proof the system is fixed or irredeemable.
- Track whether Tennessee resumes executions in 2027 with demonstrably improved venous access or contingency procedures.
- Note that pre-execution medical warnings were litigated and rejected; future cases will test whether courts treat repeated failures as new evidence.
- Primary sources (court filings, witness accounts, official statements) remain more reliable than secondary outrage narratives.

**10. What would falsify this read**

- Stanton review publicly attributes failure solely to unforeseeable individual error with no protocol or training gaps.
- Tennessee successfully executes multiple inmates in 2027 using the same or minimally tweaked protocol without further incidents.
- Pike’s condition improves dramatically with no lasting effects and she is returned to death row without successful commutation litigation.
- Internal documents emerge showing the state had clear, ignored data on chronic IV problems before September 30.

Trump’s Top 25 Achievements: The List Every Conservative Should Know and Use
Donald Trump doesn’t have an accomplishment problem. Republicans have an information problem. It’s on each of us to change that.
With the midterms coming, an astonishing number of Republican voters cannot name three things President Trump has accomplished. Which is remarkable when you consider that Donald Trump has accomplished more in a year and a half than any other president ever did in four.
Indeed, he has accomplished so much, so fast, across so many fronts that most people cannot keep up. The Enemedia buries the victories, while Republicans do an abysmal job of explaining them.
So here is the cheat sheet. It barely scratches the surface. And yet each and every item here is a game-changer, and your befuddled black-pilling friends need to know it.
This is not a list of promises. It’s a list of laws enacted, cases won, policies implemented, agreements secured, and measurable results.
You don’t have to memorize all 25. Learn five. And when somebody says Trump “hasn’t done much,” show them the receipts.
Trump Restored American Safety and Sovereignty
1. He made the border a real border again.
In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.
2. He reversed mass migration.
America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”
Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.
3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.
Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.
Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.
4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.
According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.
This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.
Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle
5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.
The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.
Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.
6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one.
In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.
Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.
7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.
That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.
No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.
8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.
9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.
10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.
Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.
11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.
Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again
12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.
Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.
Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.
13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.
In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.
14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.
Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?
15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.
What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”
16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family
17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.
Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.
He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.
No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.
Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.
19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.
That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.
20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.
Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.
Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.
23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.
24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.
Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.
25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.
Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.
Now Act Like It Matters
Those are not tweets or campaign promises. They are changes in law, power, investment, sovereignty, culture, and the structure of the Republic itself. And they’re just the top 25: I could give you hundreds more.
Midterms are turnout elections. We do not need to convince Democrats to love Donald Trump. We need Republicans and friendly independents to understand what is at stake — and to show up.
And let’s be clear. When you say (as some of you will) “the Republicans need to do a good enough job telling this story”, you’re pointing at yourself. You are “the Republicans.” The Democrats don’t rely exclusively on their elected officials to tell their story: everyone from their media lackeys to their lowest-level supporters are constantly spreading their “news”, whatever that “news” happens to be.
Today’s conservatives have more ability to find whatever you want to know than any group of people in human history, yet half of them couldn’t name any of the accomplishments in this essay, and if they were to read it, they would just complain that something else they wanted hasn’t happened fast enough to suit them.
This is called “black-pilling.” It’s a loser mindset, and if you engage in it, you deserve to lose: horribly, painfully, personally. And guess what: you will, unless people who are serious step up to save you. Which is frankly pathetic, but for the rest of our sakes, necessary.
So tell people our story. Donald Trump is delivering great things, whether or not heaven on earth has broken out quite yet. Do the work, send the team he needs to Washington to finish the job, and get ready for 2028 afterward.
Take the time to learn at least five of these victories. Share this list with someone who needs it. And vote as though the most consequential Presidency in modern history depends on what you do.
Because it does.
Rod D. Martin

text:
7 Best Poly Ash Siding Solutions for Contemporary Texas Architecture
Benjamin Baker📷
a few seconds ago
8 min read
Texas homes ask a lot from exterior materials. A wall can face blistering sun, wind-driven rain, sweeping temperature swings, insects, and the design pressure of looking clean and current from the street.That is why poly ash siding has become a serious option for contemporary residential architecture. It gives builders and designers the crisp profiles they want, while handling many of the problems that make wood, fiber cement, and some PVC details harder to use in demanding climates.Poly ash is typically made with polymers and fly ash. The result is a durable exterior material that can be cut, routed, fastened, and painted in ways that feel familiar to crews used to working with wood. For modern Texas homes, that flexibility matters.This list is ranked by how often each solution solves a real design or performance problem. The best choices combine clean lines, jobsite practicality, and long-term exterior durability.📷Poly ash siding supports sharp modern lines without making the exterior feel cold.1. Smooth horizontal lap siding for clean modern facades
Smooth horizontal lap siding is the safest starting point for contemporary Texas architecture. It works on custom homes, spec houses, lake homes, and remodels because it gives the exterior a disciplined rhythm without feeling trendy.The appeal is simple. Smooth lap siding reduces visual noise. It lets strong roof forms, dark windows, stone bases, and shaded porches do their job. Compared with wood-grain textures, a smooth poly ash face looks cleaner and more architectural.This solution works especially well on:Long street-facing elevations
Two-story modern farmhouse designs
Hill Country homes with limestone or stucco accents
Transitional homes that need a cleaner update
Garages and detached casitasA major strength of poly ash is that it can be field-cut and detailed like wood. That matters around windows, corners, and wall breaks where contemporary homes need tight, intentional lines.Practical tipUse wider exposure patterns if the architecture is simple and low-slung. Narrower exposures can work on taller elevations, but too many lines can make a facade feel busy. For most contemporary designs, restraint looks better than complexity.2. Board-and-batten siding for vertical height and shadow
Board-and-batten siding has moved far beyond farmhouse design. On a modern Texas home, vertical siding can make a simple wall feel taller, sharper, and more custom.Poly ash is a smart material for this look because vertical details are exposed to water movement, sun, and temperature changes in different ways than horizontal siding. A stable trim and siding system helps keep battens looking straight and intentional.Board-and-batten works best when it has a clear design purpose. It should not cover every surface by default. Use it to create contrast.Good placements include:Entry towers
Gable ends
Stairwell walls
Fireplace projections
Garage faces
Rear outdoor living elevationsThe vertical lines pair well with standing seam metal roofs, steel-look windows, exposed beams, and simple concrete or stone hardscape.Practical tipDo not make batten spacing an afterthought. Lay out the wall before installation so battens land cleanly around windows, doors, sconces, hose bibs, and outlets. Uneven spacing near openings can make an otherwise expensive exterior look improvised.📷Vertical siding can give a simple entry more height and presence.3. Nickel gap siding for refined porch ceilings and accent walls
Nickel gap siding gives Texas homes a refined, finished look without the heavier shadow of shiplap. It is especially useful on covered areas where people see the material up close.Think porch ceilings, outdoor kitchens, breezeway walls, cabana interiors, and protected entry alcoves. These are the places where texture and craftsmanship matter. A smooth wall may feel flat, while a nickel gap profile adds just enough line and shadow.Poly ash is a good fit here because exterior ceilings and covered walls still face humidity, insects, heat, and windblown moisture. Painted wood can look beautiful, but it often needs more upkeep in these conditions.Nickel gap also helps connect indoor and outdoor spaces. When used under a porch roof or patio cover, it brings a finished-room quality to the exterior.Practical tipUse nickel gap in focused areas rather than across the whole house. It is strongest as an accent. A porch ceiling in a warm white, soft gray, or muted natural tone can make the entire outdoor living space feel more designed.4. Wide poly ash trim for crisp window and door detailing
Contemporary architecture depends on edges. Windows, doors, corners, fascia, and panel transitions need to look crisp. If trim waves, swells, splits, or feels undersized, the whole exterior suffers.Wide poly ash trim is one of the most useful siding companions because it creates clean frames around modern openings. It can also replace more maintenance-heavy wood trim in areas exposed to sun and rain.This matters on Texas homes with dark windows, large sliders, and full-glass patio doors. These openings already draw attention. The trim around them needs to look deliberate.Good applications include:Flat window surrounds
Door casing
Inside and outside corners
Band boards between materials
Garage door trim
Fascia and rake boardsThe best contemporary trim details are usually simple. Flat profiles tend to look cleaner than heavily molded profiles. That simplicity also makes it easier to combine siding with masonry, stucco, metal, or brick.Practical tipMatch trim scale to the size of the opening. Large windows and tall doors usually need wider trim to feel balanced. Small trim around large glass can look thin and underbuilt.5. Mixed-material siding packages for stone, stucco, brick, and metal
Many contemporary Texas homes are not one-material homes. They combine siding with limestone, stucco, brick, steel, exposed wood, or metal roofing. Poly ash works well in these mixed packages because it can act as the clean connective layer.This is where thoughtful design matters most. Materials should not compete. Stone may ground the home. Stucco may simplify large wall planes. Metal may sharpen the roofline. Poly ash siding and trim can connect these pieces with clean transitions.A common approach is to use poly ash lap siding on the main body, vertical siding on feature walls, and wide trim at openings. This gives the home variety without making every elevation feel https://t.co/r3oCF2m8NS from Austin, Texas, to Dallas, San Antonio, Houston, and Travis Club often use mixed exterior palettes because regional styles vary so much. A Hill Country home may lean on stone and warm neutrals. A Houston home may need a lighter palette and strong moisture detailing. A Dallas home may use cleaner urban lines with brick or stucco.Practical tipLimit the exterior to a few main materials. Three primary materials are usually enough for a contemporary home. More than that can make the design look patched together.📷Clean transitions help mixed-material homes feel intentional.6. Dark painted poly ash siding for bold modern contrast
Dark exteriors are popular in contemporary residential design, and for good reason. Charcoal, deep bronze, black-green, and soft black siding can make a home look grounded and refined. They also pair well with light stone, pale concrete, natural wood tones, and bronze or black windows.Poly ash can be a strong candidate for dark painted siding because it accepts paint and supports crisp detailing. Still, dark colors require planning in hot climates. Any dark exterior surface absorbs more heat than a light one.That does not mean dark siding is off the table in Texas. It means the design needs smart placement.Use dark poly ash siding on:Shaded entry volumes
Rear patio walls
Upper-level masses
Accent bays
Garage doors and surrounding trim
Small modern additionsA full black exterior can be striking, but it may not be the right fit for every site. Exposure, orientation, roof overhangs, landscaping, and neighborhood context all matter.Practical tipCheck the paint manufacturer’s guidance for exterior use and heat exposure. Choose coatings designed for the substrate and climate. On large sun-facing walls, slightly softer dark tones often age more gracefully than pure black.7. Complete siding and trim systems for fewer field compromises
The strongest poly ash solution is not always a single profile. Often, it is a complete siding and trim package planned from the start.This matters because exterior problems usually happen at transitions. Corners, trim connections, window openings, rooflines, and penetrations carry more risk than the middle of a wall. When siding and trim are specified together, the installer has fewer awkward changes in thickness, texture, and movement.A complete package may include:Horizontal siding
Vertical siding
Trim boards
Corner boards
Fascia
Soffit or ceiling material
Band boards
Panel accentsThis approach gives architects, builders, and homeowners more control over the finished look. It also helps crews maintain consistent details across the home.For example, someone comparing TruExterior siding and trim US Lumber Brokers Austin may care less about one isolated board and more about how the whole exterior package comes together. That is the right way to think about poly ash. The material performs best when the design, water management, fasteners, coatings, and installation details all work as a system.Practical tipDecide on the trim package before siding installation begins. Waiting until the field crew is already solving corners and openings can lead to mismatched boards, inconsistent reveals, and rushed details.📷A complete trim package makes rooflines, corners, and openings feel connected.What makes poly ash a good match for Texas homes
Poly ash siding is not only about style. It solves practical problems that often show up in Texas construction.The biggest advantage is design flexibility. Crews can cut and fasten many poly ash products with familiar woodworking methods. That helps on custom homes where every elevation has different window sizes, trim returns, and roof https://t.co/fk3DugLWEh also offers strong resistance to common exterior threats. Unlike wood, it is not a food source for termites. It does not absorb moisture in the same way traditional wood can. It can hold crisp edges and support painted finishes, which is useful for modern architecture.Still, no siding material performs well without proper installation. Water needs a path out. Flashing must be correct. Paint and fasteners need to match manufacturer guidance. Clearances from grade, roofs, decks, and paving should be respected.A good poly ash exterior starts with design, but it lasts because the wall assembly is built https://t.co/3nx7irWRhX to choose the right poly ash siding solution
The best choice depends on the home’s architecture, exposure, and budget. A simple decision path https://t.co/TgjRubhV0b goalBest poly ash solutionClean modern street viewSmooth horizontal lap sidingTaller, sharper formBoard-and-batten sidingFinished outdoor living spaceNickel gap sidingCrisp openings and cornersWide trim packageRegional Texas characterMixed-material packageBold contemporary lookDark painted accentsBest overall consistencyComplete siding and trim systemStart with the main wall profile, then build the trim strategy around it. After that, choose accent areas. This keeps the exterior from becoming too busy.For most homes, the best overall pick is a complete poly ash siding and trim system with smooth lap siding as the base, wide trim at openings, and vertical or nickel gap accents where the architecture needs emphasis.That combination fits contemporary Texas design because it is clean, practical, and flexible. It gives the exterior enough detail to feel custom, without adding materials just for the sake of variety.Poly ash will not save a weak design or poor installation. But when the profiles, trim, paint, and water management are planned together, it can help create a Texas home that looks sharp on day one and stays easier to maintain over time.

text:
Here's today's hardtech brief!

U.S. HARDTECH:
- Aventra raised a $17.5M Series A led by Konvoy Ventures for Piranha, a kit that turns ordinary bombs into guided gliders dropped from balloons at 60k feet. With 400+ flights in under a year, CEO Michael Weigand's pitch is that "stratospheric winds carrying mass downrange without fuel get you much more range."

- Schneider Electric agreed to acquire Boston's PTC for $22.6B, a premium of more than 40%. PTC's design and product-lifecycle software runs through U.S. aerospace and auto manufacturing, and the deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2027.

- The Energy Department offered Vistra a conditional $4.2B loan to squeeze 433 MW more out of three nuclear plants in Ohio and Pennsylvania and keep about 4 GW running another 20 years. These "uprates" are the fastest way to add nuclear power, and Meta has already signed to buy the extra output. @VistraCorp 

- Colorado's Ursa Major won $137M from the Navy for solid rocket motors, including $91M for a 7-inch motor for a new compact air-to-air missile. Solid rocket motors are currently a major bottleneck in missile production and Ursa Major builds them partly with 3D printing. @ursamajortech 

- Northrop Grumman's Talon Blue drone wingman made its first flight, fully autonomously, out of Mojave. Northrop paid for it itself after missing the Air Force's first round of drone wingmen, which went to General Atomics and Anduril. Talon Blue is now aimed at the much larger second round.

- Palo Alto's SafeWorld came out of stealth with a $12M seed co-led by Shine Capital and a16z Speedrun to safety-test robots in simulation against realistic digital humans. Co-founder Ding Zhao runs Carnegie Mellon's Safe AI Lab.

- Linse Capital, the growth investor behind SpaceX, Skydio, and Impulse Space, disclosed a $75M early-stage fund plus $75M for co-investments in defense supply chain, in-space manufacturing, chipmaking, and fusion. It's mostly deployed already, in companies like Varda, Amca, and Thea Energy, a sign that growth investors are moving earlier to get access.

- Elon Musk confirmed talks with TSMC about his planned Terafab chip factory: "Just discussions, but something may come of it." Tech columnist Tim Culpan, who broke the story, says the most likely outcome is TSMC owning and operating the plant.

- The Army has downed 11 cartel drones with lasers on the Mexican border since August, while testing systems from Anduril, Teledyne FLIR, Austin's Allen Control Systems, and Powerus. Separately, Powerus landed an $82M Air Force order for its Guardian-2 interceptor drones.

- MISO, the grid operator for much of the Midwest, asked federal regulators to approve a 120-day fast track for new loads over 200 MW that bring their own power plants. If approved starting in early 2027, data centers and factories that build their own generation could connect in months instead of years.

ALLIED HARDTECH:
- European defense startups are on track to raise $10.5B this year, four times last year, according to Dealroom and Resilience Media, cutting the U.S. share of NATO-wide defense startup funding to 75%. Bessemer's Alex Ferrara says both sides share one problem: exits, because defense has only a small number of strategic acquirers.

- Oxford's Living Optics raised $20M led by BRV Capital, adding Lockheed Martin Ventures and the venture arms of chip-equipment makers Applied Materials and Lam Research. Its hyperspectral cameras, which see far more bands of light than a normal camera, target defense and industrial inspection. @LivingOptics 

- Cardiff's Reclinker raised a £10M Series A to turn cement from demolished buildings back into clinker, cement's key ingredient, inside the electric arc furnaces steelmakers already run. It says the process cuts emissions about 50% at no extra cost and plans to expand to steel sites in Europe and the U.S.

Follow for more hardtech news!

So in 1948, as Britain was leaving, the Arab population was just sitting around with pencils & paper eager to create a new political entity with their Jewish neighbors? That's some strong Humboldt County you're  smoking!

Ben Gurion pleaded with Arabs to stay. Many did. Others did not at the urging of Arab states. 

Why does Israel (and Egypt) maintain that quarantine?  Because in 2002 during the Second Intifada, shortly after Arafat signed Oslo and renounced violence, he was caught smuggling weapons into Gaza on the Karin A.

When Sharon pulled out of Gaza in 2005 he had every intention to gradually ease the quarantine provided the PLO agreed to security. But then Hamas took over, refused to recognize Israel or renounce violence and began a series of wars by firing rockets & artillery over the border killing Israeli civilians.

There may have been smuggling tunnels into Egypt or Israel, but you're deluded if you think 300 miles of tunnels throughout the territory were needed to smuggle in consumer goods.

Yes the Area C arrangement was temporary. But all peace proposals since Oslo recognized there needed to be land swaps or other compensation for the blocs. Clinton's plan did this, as did Olmert's, as did Trump's. Obama got nowhere. Abbas rejected them out of hand.

Under no scenario is Israel going to redivide Jerusalem, evacuate 700,000 of its citizens, or dismantle cities like Ariel, Gush Etzion or Ma'ale Adumim. 

The 1947 Partition Plan would have meant full sovereignty. After the 1967 war Israel offered to return all the territories in exchange for peace. The Arab states responded with their famous "three no's" from Khartoum (that is in Sudan by the way, who normalized relations with Israel under the Abraham Accords).

The best Palestinians can hope for now is to make Areas A/B exclaves of Jordan with a landbridge connecting them. Area C is gone. 

I am not full of hate. But I do detest those who purposely murder innocent civilians, especially children. Like these two Israeli boys. Daniel was 4 years old when he was killed in his driveway as his family was evacuating from Hamas artillery. Ido was 5 years old when a Hamas rocket destroyed his apartment. Senseless deaths.

text:
Every interview about Elon Musk's personal life asks the same questions. Why did the marriages end. What went wrong with Amber. How does he manage 12 children. What does he regret.

Nobody asks the question that matters most: does he believe he is capable of being loved for who he is without the companies.

Not the rockets. Not the billions. Not the vision. Not the genius. The man underneath all of it. The man who sits in a room after the employees go home and the interviews end and the phone stops buzzing. Does that man believe someone could love him. Just him. The version with nothing to offer except his presence.

The answer is visible in the structure of every relationship he's built. The acquisition phase delivers the full force of his value proposition: attention, resources, vision, intensity. The offering is so overwhelming that the woman cannot separate the man from the offering. By the time she tries, the offering has withdrawn and the man underneath has never been properly introduced.

He doesn't let the man underneath be known because the man underneath is the boy from Pretoria who was told by his father that he was inadequate and was told by his peers through violence that he was unacceptable. The companies were built as proof of adequacy. The wealth was built as proof of value. The mission was built as proof of importance. All of it addresses the original wound: you are not enough.

The wound runs a program: if they see the real me, they'll leave. So he offers the extraordinary version. The version nobody leaves because nobody walks away from rockets and billions and the future of civilization. But the extraordinary version is a character. The man inside the character is tired and lonely and sends memes at 2am because he can't sleep and wants someone to be there.

Every relationship has been an attempt to answer the question nobody asks. And every relationship has ended before the answer could arrive because the question was never allowed to be spoken.

The man who is building a future for 8 billion people has never resolved the question of whether one person could love him without it.

“𝘐𝘵’𝘴 𝘩𝘢𝘳𝘥 𝘣𝘦𝘤𝘢𝘶𝘴𝘦 𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘨𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘩𝘰𝘮𝘦, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘐’𝘮 𝘱𝘰𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘭𝘦𝘴𝘴,” Andrew Rose told FOX 11 Los Angeles about his 92-year-old father, Howard. Ventura County now holds conservatorship over the man, and the family says it got there through a lie.

According to the family, a hospital visit ended in false accusations that they had abandoned Howard. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐲 𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧, 𝐭𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐥, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐡𝐢𝐦 𝐢𝐧 𝐚 𝐧𝐮𝐫𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 that the family says has a record of 129 documented elder abuse cases.

The family says the county then imposed palliative care despite treatable symptoms. A feeding tube decision rested on one “failed” swallow test that the family says Howard actually passed, and they say the county refused independent evaluations offered by Cedars-Sinai and UCLA.

Now the family says the county is going after the condo they live in to cover bills they dispute owing. “𝘞𝘦 𝘩𝘢𝘥 𝘯𝘰 𝘤𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘭 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵𝘴; 𝘩𝘦 𝘩𝘢𝘥 𝘯𝘰 𝘥𝘶𝘦 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘴𝘴,” Cynthia Rose said. 𝐀 𝐟𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐰𝐡𝐨 𝐰𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐠𝐨 𝐡𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐧’𝐭, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐲 𝐰𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲’𝐬 𝐡𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐩𝐚𝐲 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐢𝐭.

These are the family’s allegations, as reported by FOX 11, and the county’s side is not laid out in the report. But if this can happen to one 92-year-old with a son at his bedside, ask what a county could do to your parents.

text:
Britain is not a Christian country. The people insisting it is are almost always on the far right, and they are not making a historical claim. They are drawing a border.
Ask them what they mean and the answer collapses. It’s not the Church of England, or they would have to explain why establishment stops at the Tweed. And it’s not the Kirk. It definitely isn’t the census, nor the empty pews on a Sunday. It’s not the Reformation, when this country last took Christianity seriously enough to decide which Christians counted and punished the rest. They offer no date, no doctrine, and no denominator. The phrase only ever gets thrown around as a way of saying who doesn’t belong: Muslims, migrants, anyone who won’t perform the right nostalgia. It’s a far-right slogan stapled to the book of (not very) common prayer.
The other move is worse. Religion treated as a synonym for morality, as if decency were leased from God and expired without Him. It isn’t. You don’t need a deity to know that cruelty is wrong, that a promise binds, that hurting someone weaker than you is contemptible. Atheists manage this every day without a choir. The far right’s public piety is not evidence of virtue. It’s costume. Plenty of the loudest believers keep the sermon for daylight and the damage for after dark.
It’s seven on a Monday evening and from my balcony I can hear the peal of church bells like surround-sound in the middle of Catholic Poland. That’s not evensong in a Kent village, and it’s still never been the source of right and wrong.

text:
Closer to negligent, or a judgment that aged badly
•  Early mask guidance. The February 5, 2020 email to Sylvia Burwell — drugstore masks are for source control and “not really effective in keeping out virus” — is real, but it is an email, not a diary entry. On March 8 he told 60 Minutes there was no reason to walk around in a mask. On March 31 the diary says “we probably were too strong in saying masks do not work.” That is the opposite of a private belief that masks were useless. The early line mixed a real supply shortage with overconfident claims about efficacy. Presenting a shortage rationale as settled science was a messaging failure; the diary itself treats the “masks don’t work” line as the error.
•  The fatality-rate numbers. On February 8, 2020, he and Tom Frieden agreed the case fatality rate was more like 0.2–0.3 percent once undetected infections were counted, “a bad influenza.” On March 11 he told Congress the stated mortality was about 3 percent, and that counting mild and asymptomatic cases probably brought it to about 1 percent, “10 times more lethal than the seasonal flu.” He did flag the asymptomatic adjustment. The gap between his private 0.2–0.3 and the 1 percent he offered Congress is real, but both were estimates under bad Chinese data. Overconfident, not a diary proof that he invented a number.
•  Six-foot distancing and child masking. In 2024 testimony he said the six-foot rule “sort of just appeared” from CDC, and that there had been no study of masks on children before the guidance. That is institutional negligence dressed up as science, not something the diary shows him fabricating.
•  Prolonged school closures and transmission claims for the vaccines. The diary shows him arguing by August 2020 that opening schools should be the default and that bars should close before schools. The broader public-health posture — long closures, and 2021 claims that vaccination would stop infection and transmission — outran the evidence. Those were overconfident forecasts, later walked back, not diary entries in which he says he knew they were false.
The diary is strongest on the gap between private uncertainty and public certainty: origins in February 2020, the muzzling denial, the booster interval, and the 2022 school-closure rewrite. It is weak as proof of a single planned deception. A lot of the rest is the ordinary failure mode of the pandemic response: early calls made with thin data, then defended as if they had been settled science.

text:
I just read where Gary Lineker said Declan Rice’s place in the England team isn’t assured anymore and honestly, I had to laugh.

Just a few days ago, we were hearing similar arguments about Saliba and whether his place in the France team was guaranteed. Now it’s Rice’s turn?

And apparently Scott could take over Rice’s place because he gives England more control and calmness. Lol. So Rice doesn’t give you control and calmness?

I feel like this is judging the whole thing purely from what England look like when they have the ball. But football doesn’t work like that. What happens when England lose possession? What happens when they need someone to cover ground, win duels, protect the defence and deal with transitions?

That’s where I struggle with this argument.

Can Scott cover the amount of ground Rice covers? Can he provide the same physical presence? Can he win the same number of duels and recover the ball as consistently? Can he give England the same defensive protection while still contributing in possession?

Rice is also someone who has played in huge games for club and country. He has Champions League experience, international tournament experience and has already played in some of the biggest matches you can possibly play.

And I’m not saying Scott is a bad player. Far from it. He has qualities that can give England something different, especially in possession. But saying that means Rice’s place is suddenly under serious threat feels like a massive conclusion to draw from a few matches.

For me, Rice offers England a balance that is difficult to replace. His value isn't only about what he does when England have the ball. It’s everything he does when they don’t have it too.

You can talk about control and calmness all you want, but when the game becomes chaotic, when England need someone to cover space, win the ball, make a recovery run or put his body on the line, Rice is exactly the kind of midfielder you want.
